cues.en: [APPLAUSE]
cues.zh: [掌声]

cues.en: JENNIFER: Thank you so much. I am going to open by saying that, I am a huge, huge fan of physics history;
cues.zh: JENNIFER：非常感谢。我想先说一句，我是物理学史的超级超级粉丝；

cues.en: I am well-aquainted with this famous room, and I am completely intimidated and unworthy.
cues.zh: 我对这间著名的报告厅很熟悉，心里完全被镇住了，觉得自己不够格。

cues.en: But we are all here for the same reason; because we love science, and I am especially honoured that
cues.zh: 但我们来这里都是同一个原因：因为我们热爱科学。我尤其感到荣幸的是，

cues.en: I get to give the first joint talk with my own husband, Sean Carroll.
cues.zh: 我能和我自己的丈夫 Sean Carroll 做第一次联合演讲。

cues.en: This is the kind of thing we talk about at home, and it's the first time that we've actually both talked about this topic.
cues.zh: 这其实就是我们家里聊的话题，这也是我们俩第一次一起公开谈这个话题。

cues.en: So, you are kind of in for a first.
cues.zh: 所以，你接下来会有点新鲜感。

cues.en: Ultimately, this is a story about Alice and Bob. Alice and Bob, for those of you who don't know,
cues.zh: 说到底，这是一个关于 Alice 和 Bob 的故事。Alice 和 Bob，可能有些人还不知道，

cues.en: are kind of fixtures when it comes to thought experiments, particularly those involving information theory,
cues.zh: 在思想实验里算是常客了，尤其是涉及信息论的，

cues.en: cartography, and especially quantum information in cartography.
cues.zh: 地图绘制，特别是量子信息在地图绘制中的应用。

cues.en: It just seems a little more fun to play around with the ideas of these actual two characters, Bob and Alice,
cues.zh: 拿 Bob 和 Alice 这两个真实角色来玩味这些想法，似乎更有趣一些，

cues.en: and the different adventures that they get into.
cues.zh: 还有他们经历的各种冒险。

cues.en: The subject tonight, Black hole Firewalls, is another kind of thought experiment that physicists started to play around with,
cues.zh: 今晚的主题——黑洞火墙——是物理学家开始探讨的另一种思想实验，

cues.en: around the questions of what happens when that daredevil Alice, who the the more risk taking of the two,
cues.zh: 围绕的问题是：当那个爱冒险的 Alice——两人中更敢冒险的那位——

cues.en: jumps into a black hole.
cues.zh: 跳进黑洞时，会发生什么。

cues.en: You know, Bob kind of stays behind.
cues.zh: 你知道，Bob 算是留在外面。

cues.en: Now, there's been a traditional way of thinking about this, sort of standard textbook, popular science, physics stuff for decades,
cues.zh: 几十年来，关于这个问题一直有种传统思路，算是标准教科书和科普物理里的说法，

cues.en: that we thought we knew pretty well what happened,
cues.zh: 我们以为自己相当清楚会发生什么，

cues.en: that she would be ripped to shreds by the power of gravity at the singularity,
cues.zh: 她会在奇点处被引力撕成碎片，

cues.en: that point of infinite density at the black hole centre.
cues.zh: 也就是黑洞中心那个密度无限大的点。

cues.en: But when the physicists started playing around, in the summer of 2012,
cues.zh: 但2012年夏天，物理学家们开始琢磨，

cues.en: with some of the big ideas of one of the other thought experiments that deals with information laws,
cues.zh: 另一个涉及信息定律的思想实验中的一些重要观点，

cues.en: they actually discovered a paradox. They discovered that it was possible that instead of being ripped to shreds by gravity,
cues.zh: 结果他们真的发现了一个悖论。他们发现，有可能爱丽丝不会被引力撕成碎片，

cues.en: Alice might be burnt up alive in this enormous wall of radiation just in the event horizon. She never even gets the chance to be ripped apart to shreds.
cues.zh: 而是在事件视界处被这堵巨大的辐射墙活活烧死。她甚至根本没机会被撕成碎片。

cues.en: So this talk is about that. And we are going to start off easy and slow,
cues.zh: 所以这次演讲要讲的就是这个。我们先从简单、缓慢的内容开始，

cues.en: but it's going to get mind-bending towards the end.
cues.zh: 但到最后会变得非常烧脑。

cues.en: The good news is, you have Sean Carroll doing the really mind-bending stuff and he is a tremendous communicator.
cues.zh: 好消息是，真正烧脑的部分由 Sean Carroll 来讲，而他是位极出色的表达者。

cues.en: So, a paradox, for those of you who want a definition: "a statement that apparently contradicts itself and yet might be true. "
cues.zh: 那么，什么是悖论？给需要定义的人一个定义：“一个表面上自相矛盾、却可能为真的陈述。”

cues.en: In physics, they are quite commonly used; this is a maybe not that specific definition. It is more that they are revealed by though experiments,
cues.zh: 在物理学中，悖论用得相当普遍；这个定义可能没那么精确。更准确地说，它们是通过思想实验展现出来的，

cues.en: and they are used to eliminate certain counter-intuitive truths, to reveal flaws in the assumptions or in the logic behind some of the reasoning in physics.
cues.zh: 并被用来排除某些反直觉的结论，揭示物理学中某些推理背后假设或逻辑上的漏洞。

cues.en: So there is a long tradition in this, and it goes all the way back to the Zeno's paradoxes, including Archilles and the tortoise,
cues.zh: 这类讨论由来已久，可以一直追溯到芝诺悖论，包括阿基里斯和乌龟。

cues.en: how the fleet Archilles can give the tortoise a head start, and although Archilles can run so much faster he never quite catches up.
cues.zh: 飞毛腿阿基里斯让乌龟先跑一段，尽管阿基里斯跑得快得多，他却始终追不上乌龟。

cues.en: It became a foundation of calculus, figuring out what the limit was in calculus.
cues.zh: 这成了微积分的基础，也就是搞清楚微积分里的极限是什么。

cues.en: Maxwell's daemon was used to illuminate thoughts on entropy and thermodynamics.
cues.zh: 麦克斯韦妖被用来启发人们对熵和热力学的思考。

cues.en: In special relativity, Einstein came up with a Twin paradox: what happens when one twin stays behind on earth,
cues.zh: 在狭义相对论中，爱因斯坦提出了双生子悖论：当一个双胞胎留在地球上，

cues.en: and the other twin zips off into space, at speed of light. When that twin comes back, he will be much younger than the twin he left behind.
cues.zh: 而另一个双胞胎以光速飞向太空。当这个双胞胎回来时，他会比留在地球上的那个双胞胎年轻得多。

cues.en: That is a paradox, and it illuminates certain factors of special relativity.
cues.zh: 那是一个悖论，它也阐明了狭义相对论的某些因素。

cues.en: Tonight, we are going to focus on a lot of the quantum mechanical paradoxes. Sean will be telling you about the Schrodinger's cat paradox.
cues.zh: 今晚，我们将重点讨论许多量子力学悖论。Sean 会给大家讲薛定谔的猫悖论。

cues.en: He will be mentioning Heisenberg uncertainty principle. Central to this entire thing, is the Black hole information paradox.
cues.zh: 他会提到海森堡不确定性原理。整个问题的核心，是黑洞信息悖论。

cues.en: It is in fact, the thing out of which Black hole firewalls came.
cues.zh: 事实上，黑洞防火墙正是由此而来。

cues.en: But first, a little bit on the history of Black holes. I'd like to do this because, as I said, I love physics history.
cues.zh: 但首先，简单讲讲黑洞的历史。我这么做是因为，我说过，我很喜欢物理学史。

cues.en: And I also love this guy, John Michell.
cues.zh: 我也很喜欢这个人，John Michell。

cues.en: He was basically an English rector in the 18th century. Common descriptions of him at that time basically stated that
cues.zh: 他基本上是18世纪英国的一位教区长。当时对他的常见描述基本上是说，

cues.en: he was "short swarthy and fat".
cues.zh: 他“矮小、肤色黝黑、身材肥胖”。

cues.en: But he was known as a brilliant thinker, and in fact, he was far more brilliant than his contemporaries realised,
cues.zh: 但他以思想卓越著称，事实上，他远比同时代人意识到的还要卓越，

cues.en: because he was literally 150 years ahead of his time.
cues.zh: 因为他实际上领先了他的时代整整150年。

cues.en: He was trying to figure out, one day, how you could calculate the mass of a star.
cues.zh: 有一天，他试图弄清楚如何计算一颗恒星的质量。

cues.en: And he came up with this method, you know, thinking that he could basically measure the reduction of the speed of light that was being emitted by it.
cues.zh: 他想出了这个方法，你知道，觉得基本上可以通过测量它发出的光速减慢多少来做到。

cues.en: And his thinking was very Newtonian. Remember, at this point in time, the debate over whether light was a particle, a wave was still going on.
cues.zh: 他的思路非常牛顿式。记住，在当时，关于光究竟是粒子还是波的争论仍在继续。

cues.en: He very much described, in Newton's notion that, light was a particle, or a "core puzzle", as I think Newton called them.
cues.zh: 他很大程度上是在阐述牛顿的观点：光是一种粒子，或者按牛顿的说法，我记得叫“微粒”。

cues.en: So he thought that gravity would slow down the light, and he could basically measure how much the light was slowing down;
cues.zh: 所以他认为引力会让光减速，而他基本能测出光究竟慢了多少；

cues.en: he could use that to calculate the mass, through a series of calculation.
cues.zh: 再通过一系列计算，他就能用这个算出质量。

cues.en: He also had another insight: when he actually started doing the maths, he realised that at some some point,
cues.zh: 他还有另一个洞见：当他真正开始做数学推导时，他意识到在某个点上，

cues.en: gravity would become so strong that the escape velocity would exceed the speed of light.
cues.zh: 引力会强到让逃逸速度超过光速。

cues.en: The escape velocity is what happens ---- say when you fire a cannon, and it was a famous thought experiment by Newton to describe gravity - how objects orbit.
cues.zh: 逃逸速度讲的是这样一种情况——比如你发射一颗炮弹，这是牛顿为描述引力、解释物体如何绕轨运行而提出的著名思想实验。

cues.en: They are basically in free fall, if you escape the earth's atmosphere, you'd go into near-earth orbit.
cues.zh: 它们基本上处于自由落体状态；一旦脱离地球大气层，你就会进入近地轨道。

cues.en: An object, a space station, satellite are just constantly in free fall around the earth.
cues.zh: 物体、空间站、卫星，其实都一直在绕地球做自由落体运动。

cues.en: But you need to be able to get beyond that; you'd need to be able to escape that part.
cues.zh: 但你需要能够越过这个范围；你需要能够逃出那一部分。

cues.en: So what happens if light can't escape? Then we wouldn't even be able to see the star.
cues.zh: 如果光无法逃逸会怎样？那我们甚至根本看不到那颗恒星。

cues.en: So he called it a "dark star", and he also had another key insight:
cues.zh: 于是他称之为“暗星”，而且他还有另一个关键洞见：

cues.en: he thought: well maybe you couldn't see it directly, but it might have a twin star near it that was bright,
cues.zh: 他想：也许你没法直接看到它，但它附近可能有一颗明亮的伴星，

cues.en: and you could look at that star, and kind of figure out that there was a dark star next to it.
cues.zh: 你可以观察那颗星，从而大致推断出旁边有一颗暗星。

cues.en: He was actually wrong about how to calculate the mass of a star, because as we now know, the speed of light is constant, that's thanks to Einstein.
cues.zh: 他计算恒星质量的方法其实是错的，因为我们现在知道，光速是恒定的，这要归功于爱因斯坦。

cues.en: so there is no way you could have used that to calculate the mass of a star.
cues.zh: 所以，你根本不可能用那个来计算恒星的质量。

cues.en: But he was absolutely right about dark stars.
cues.zh: 但他在暗星这一点上完全正确。

cues.en: Unfortunately, he dies in complete obscurity; nobody took him seriously - they thought he was crazy.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，他去世时完全默默无闻；没人认真对待他——大家都觉得他疯了。

cues.en: This was so ahead of anything anyone had ever thought about, that they thought there's no way that he could possibly be right.
cues.zh: 这远远超前于当时任何人的想法，以至于大家认为他绝不可能是对的。

cues.en: He was not the only one, however. Pierre Simon LaPlace actually came to a similar conclusion a few years later,
cues.zh: 不过，他并不是唯一一个。几年后，Pierre Simon LaPlace 实际上也得出了类似的结论，

cues.en: and he talked about it in his book: Exposition du Systeme du Monde, where he basically concluded that it is possible
cues.zh: 他在自己的书《Exposition du Systeme du Monde》里谈到了这一点，基本上得出结论：有可能

cues.en: that "the greatest luminous bodies in the universe are " on this account "invisible".
cues.zh: “宇宙中最庞大的发光天体”因此“是看不见的”。

cues.en: And again, he also was right.
cues.zh: 而且，他又说对了。

cues.en: So it would basically take another 100 years, or over 100 years before we finally had Albert Einstein
cues.zh: 所以基本上还要再过 100 年，或者说 100 多年，才终于有了 Albert Einstein

cues.en: re-envisioning space-time.
cues.zh: 重新构想时空。

cues.en: Remember, in Newtonian days, they thought of space as three-dimensional, Euclidean geometry space,
cues.zh: 记住，在牛顿时代，人们认为空间是三维的、欧几里得几何空间，

cues.en: and it was static; it didn't move.
cues.zh: 而且是静态的；它不动。

cues.en: Einstein kind of re-envisioned it.
cues.zh: Einstein 某种程度上重新构想了它。

cues.en: There were three dimensions of space, and the fourth of time, and they combine to give you space-time.
cues.zh: 空间有三个维度，第四个是时间，它们结合起来就得到了时空。

cues.en: It became dynamic.
cues.zh: 它变成了动态的。

cues.en: It could twist and warp, and the things that did the warping and twisting were the massive objects in space.
cues.zh: 它可以扭曲、弯折，而让它扭曲和弯折的，是太空中那些巨大的物体。

cues.en: And that is where gravity comes from. Gravity is less a force and more say,
cues.zh: 引力正是由此而来。引力与其说是一种力，不如说是

cues.en: objects and light following the curvature of space.
cues.zh: 物体和光沿着空间的曲率运动。

cues.en: It was revolutionary; I don't think I need to tell any of you that.
cues.zh: 这是革命性的；我想我不用再跟你们强调这一点。

cues.en: It changed everything, and among the lives it changed was a physicist named Karl Schwarzschild.
cues.zh: 它改变了一切，而在它改变的人生中，有一位物理学家，名叫 Karl Schwarzschild。

cues.en: At the age of forty, he enlisted to fight in World War One, even though he was much older than some of the men out there.
cues.zh: 四十岁时，他入伍参加第一次世界大战，尽管他比战场上的一些人年长得多。

cues.en: And it was, as you might imagine, a dreadful time in the trenches, dodging bullets, bombs, bayonets, and the whole bit.
cues.zh: 正如你能想象的，在战壕里躲子弹、炸弹、刺刀，诸如此类，那段日子糟透了。

cues.en: And one of the ways that he escaped the horror of the war was to do physics.
cues.zh: 他逃避战争恐怖的一种方式，就是研究物理。

cues.en: He came upon Einstein's theory of general relativity, general theory of relativity.
cues.zh: 他接触到了爱因斯坦的广义相对论，广义相对论。

cues.en: And he became fascinated. In his spare time, he actually started working with some of the equations.
cues.zh: 他着了迷。空闲时，他真的开始研究其中一些方程。

cues.en: He was basically trying to do something similar to what Newton did.
cues.zh: 他基本上是在尝试做类似牛顿做过的事。

cues.en: Newton would measure the distance between the centre of mass of an object and another point in space.
cues.zh: 牛顿会测量物体质心与空间中另一点之间的距离。

cues.en: and as you got closer and closer, eventually you would get down to a point.
cues.zh: 随着你越来越靠近，最终会落到一个点上。

cues.en: Schwarzschild was trying to calculate the curvature of space. He hit a roadblock too, but it was well below zero.
cues.zh: Schwarzschild 也在尝试计算空间曲率。他也遇到了障碍，只不过这个障碍远低于零。

cues.en: He basically hit a point where the equation just blew up.
cues.zh: 他基本上碰到了一个点，方程在那里直接爆掉了。

cues.en: Nobody knew why. They didn't know what that point was.
cues.zh: 没人知道为什么。也没人知道那个点是什么。

cues.en: Today I think we would call it the event horizon of a black hole.
cues.zh: 今天我想我们会把它称为黑洞的事件视界。

cues.en: What we think now is that there might be something beyond that point,
cues.zh: 现在我们认为，那个点之外可能还有东西，

cues.en: even though the equations stop at that point.
cues.zh: 尽管方程在那个点就终止了。

cues.en: The good news is, John Wheeler dubbed these objects "Blacks holes" in 1968,
cues.zh: 好消息是，John Wheeler 在 1968 年把这些天体称为“黑洞”，

cues.en: and shortly after that, we found compelling evidence that in fact, they do exist.
cues.zh: 不久之后，我们就找到了有力证据，证明它们确实存在。

cues.en: The first object that they discovered that could be a candidate black hole, was this X-ray binary star Cygnus X-1.
cues.zh: 他们发现的第一个可能是黑洞候选者的天体，是这个 X 射线双星 Cygnus X-1。

cues.en: They found it, or they determined it in 1971, that there was no way it could be a neutron star.
cues.zh: 1971年他们发现，或者说确定了，它不可能是中子星。

cues.en: It was far too dense, and it was probably going to be a Black hole.
cues.zh: 它的密度太大了，很可能是个黑洞。

cues.en: And we know it was a binary star system, so Michell was absolutely right.
cues.zh: 我们知道它是双星系统，所以 Michell 完全说对了。

cues.en: They could tell the Black hole was there based on its companion star and its behaviours.
cues.zh: 他们通过伴星及其运动规律判断出黑洞就在那里。

cues.en: This lovely animation here is based on actual data Sean found on the internet, a beautiful place, the internet.
cues.zh: 这段精美的动画基于 Sean 在网上找到的真实数据——互联网，真是个美妙的地方。

cues.en: This is the black hole, at the centre of our Milky Way Galaxy.
cues.zh: 这就是黑洞，位于我们银河系的中心。

cues.en: What they had done is basically extrapolate well advancing through time, into the future,
cues.zh: 他们所做的，基本上就是沿着时间向前推演，

cues.en: to look at how the presence of the Black hole affects the movement of the bodies around it.
cues.zh: 去观察黑洞的存在如何影响它周围天体的运动。

cues.en: So Black holes, they are real, they are out there, they are probably at the centre of most galaxies.
cues.zh: 所以黑洞是真实存在的，它们就在那里，而且很可能位于大多数星系的中心。

cues.en: So now, we get back to Alice.
cues.zh: 现在我们回到 Alice。

cues.en: Because really this is all about Alice.
cues.zh: 因为说到底，这一切都是关于 Alice 的。

cues.en: Bob is kind of a smaller player on the side there.
cues.zh: Bob算是那边的一个小角色。

cues.en: Black holes have some really interesting properties.
cues.zh: 黑洞有一些非常有趣的性质。

cues.en: We know that they have immense gravity, but what happens when she crosses the event horizon?
cues.zh: 我们知道它们有巨大的引力，但当她越过事件视界时会发生什么？

cues.en: The event horizon is what Schwarzschild unknowingly discovered.
cues.zh: 事件视界正是Schwarzschild在不知情中发现的。

cues.en: It's basically the point of no return; once you cross that point, you are done; you are not getting back.
cues.zh: 它基本上是有去无回的点；一旦越过那个点，你就完了；你回不来了。

cues.en: No light can escape, no information or anything can get out of that.
cues.zh: 没有光能逃逸，任何信息或物质都无法从中逃出。

cues.en: Alice doesn't know it, because she isn't going to noticing anything unusual
cues.zh: Alice 并不知道，因为她不会注意到任何异常

cues.en: as she crosses it, but she is pretty much doomed at that point.
cues.zh: 她穿过它的时候，到那一刻她基本已经注定完蛋了。

cues.en: She just might not know it for a bit.
cues.zh: 只是她可能暂时还不会知道。

cues.en: Why is she doomed? Well, it's something that physicists like to call "no drama",
cues.zh: 她为什么注定完蛋？这涉及物理学家喜欢称为“无戏剧性”的东西，

cues.en: and it's based on Einstein's equivalence principle, this notion that gravity and acceleration are essentially the same thing.
cues.zh: 它基于爱因斯坦的等效原理：引力和加速度本质上是同一回事。

cues.en: What that means is, an object in free fall, and Alice is in free fall, does not feel the effects of gravity.
cues.zh: 意思是，自由下落的物体——Alice 就在自由下落——感受不到引力的作用。

cues.en: She's not going to notice any extreme effect. She is just going to be floating along, thinking that space is the same as it's always been.
cues.zh: 她不会注意到任何极端效应。她只会一路漂浮，觉得空间和一直以来一样。

cues.en: Until...
cues.zh: 直到……

cues.en: But first, that's from her perspective.
cues.zh: 但首先，这是从她的视角来看。

cues.en: Remember that we are taking about relativity, which means that frames of reference are important.
cues.zh: 记住，我们讲的是相对论，这意味着参考系很重要。

cues.en: Bob watches her slightly form a distance jumping into a Black hole, but what he sees is a bit different.
cues.zh: Bob 从稍远处看着她跳进黑洞，但他看到的有点不一样。

cues.en: He sees her getting slower and slower, because time slows down. Time dilates as you get closer to a black hole,
cues.zh: 他看到她的动作越来越慢，因为时间变慢了。越靠近黑洞，时间就越膨胀，

cues.en: because of the extreme effects of gravity,
cues.zh: 这是由于引力的极端效应，

cues.en: As she approaches the event horizon, she will seem to be moving slower and slower,
cues.zh: 当她接近事件视界时，她的运动看起来会越来越慢，

cues.en: and right at the end, she is just going to seem to be frozen in space to him.
cues.zh: 而到最后，在他眼中，她就像凝固在太空中。

cues.en: and that's where time ends for him, as far as Bob is concerned, and he doesn't really know what happens beyond that point.
cues.zh: 对 Bob 来说，他的时间到此就结束了；过了这一点，他根本不知道会发生什么。

cues.en: For Alice, it's bad news,
cues.zh: 对 Alice 来说，这是坏消息，

cues.en: because there is an evil singularity lurking there at the centre.
cues.zh: 因为中心潜伏着一个邪恶的奇点。

cues.en: She drifts along, and she drifts along; she is in free fall, and after a while she notices an uncomfortable tugging.
cues.zh: 她一路飘着，一路飘着；她处于自由落体状态，过了一会儿，她感到一阵不舒服的拉扯。

cues.en: that she's being stretched.
cues.zh: 原来自己正在被拉伸。

cues.en: That is because she is falling feet-first towards this singularity.
cues.zh: 这是因为她正脚朝前朝这个奇点坠落。

cues.en: At this point there is really only one way she could go, and it's towards her doom, towards the singularity.
cues.zh: 到这一步，她其实只有一个方向可去，那就是走向毁灭，走向奇点。

cues.en: it's just sort of like a...That's the only way she can travel.
cues.zh: 这有点像……那是她唯一能走的路。

cues.en: The gravity on her feet becomes stronger and stronger, much much stronger than the gravity on her head.
cues.zh: 她脚处的引力越来越强，比头处的引力强太多太多。

cues.en: So it keeps pulling and pulling, and she gets longer and longer
cues.zh: 于是它不停地拉啊拉，她也就变得越来越长，

cues.en: until she's basically...I think Kip Thorne called it being spaghettified.
cues.zh: 直到她基本上……我记得 Kip Thorne 把这叫做被“意大利面化”。

cues.en: Finally when she gets close enough to the singularity, she is just ripped to shreds,
cues.zh: 最后，当她离奇点足够近时，她就被撕成了碎片，

cues.en: and there is nothing left of poor Alice.
cues.zh: 可怜的 Alice 什么都没剩下。

cues.en: Again, poor Bob never knows the horror that awaited his partner.
cues.zh: 可怜的 Bob 又一次永远不知道等待着他同伴的恐怖。

cues.en: Of course, this is not the end of the story.
cues.zh: 当然，故事并没有到此结束。

cues.en: This is a classical view of a Black hole according to Einstein's relativity.
cues.zh: 这是根据爱因斯坦相对论对黑洞的经典看法。

cues.en: Things get really complicated with quantum mechanics, and quantum mechanics actually is relevant here,
cues.zh: 量子力学让事情变得非常复杂，而量子力学在这里其实很关键，

cues.en: because there are two different rule books for different size scales when it comes to physics.
cues.zh: 因为在物理学中，不同尺度有两套不同的规则手册。

cues.en: General relativity governs the macro-scale, the very large, the movement of the planet, things like that, you know, everyday physics.
cues.zh: 广义相对论支配宏观尺度，也就是非常大的尺度，行星的运动之类，你懂的，日常物理。

cues.en: Quantum mechanics governs the world of subatomic particles and the very small.
cues.zh: 量子力学支配亚原子粒子的世界，也就是极小的尺度。

cues.en: Those of you who are familiar with the discovery of Higgs boson will know that
cues.zh: 熟悉希格斯玻色子发现的人会知道，

cues.en: that was the last piece in what's known as the standard model of particle physics.
cues.zh: 那是粒子物理学标准模型的最后一块拼图。

cues.en: That model is now complete.
cues.zh: 这个模型现在完整了。

cues.en: Except for one bit: that model doesn't include gravity.
cues.zh: 只差一点：这个模型不包含引力。

cues.en: Gravity and quantum mechanics just don't play well together,
cues.zh: 引力和量子力学就是合不来，

cues.en: and physicists are yet to devise a quantum theory of gravity that works.
cues.zh: 而物理学家尚未提出一个可行的量子引力理论。

cues.en: Blackholes, because they are basically where relativity and quantum mechanics meet,
cues.zh: 黑洞基本上是相对论和量子力学交汇的地方，

cues.en: that's why they are tremendously interesting to physicists.
cues.zh: 所以它们对物理学家来说极其有趣。

cues.en: So surprise. this is something we find out when we start to apply quantum mechanics to black holes.
cues.zh: 所以，令人意外的是，这正是我们开始把量子力学应用到黑洞上时发现的东西。

cues.en: Stephen Hawking, playing around with this in 1970s, came up with this idea of Hawking radiation.
cues.zh: Stephen Hawking 在20世纪70年代琢磨这个问题时，提出了霍金辐射这个概念。

cues.en: Turns out that Black holes are not completely black.
cues.zh: 事实证明，黑洞并不完全是黑的。

cues.en: That's partly because, empty space, when you are talking quantum mechanically, is not really empty.
cues.zh: 部分原因是，从量子力学角度看，真空其实并不是真的空。

cues.en: Space-time is really...you've got these virtual particles that are popping in and out of existence,
cues.zh: 时空其实……有这些虚粒子不断凭空出现又消失，

cues.en: antimatter and matter, Alice and Bob,
cues.zh: 反物质和物质，Alice 和 Bob，

cues.en: and what happens when they meet is that they annihilate into energy almost instantaneously,
cues.zh: 当它们相遇时，几乎瞬间就会湮灭成能量，

cues.en: so they don't violate the conservation of energy; they are not around long enough.
cues.zh: 所以它们并不违反能量守恒；它们存在的时间不够长。

cues.en: Nonetheless, space-time at the quantum level is this kind of bubbly frothy foam, so to speak.
cues.zh: 不过，量子层面的时空可以说是这种冒泡、翻腾的泡沫。

cues.en: So what happens when these virtual particle pairs, Alice and Bob,
cues.zh: 那么，当这些虚粒子对——Alice 和 Bob——

cues.en: pop up into existence right at the event horizon of a Black hole?
cues.zh: 恰好在黑洞的事件视界处凭空出现时，会发生什么？

cues.en: Alice is just a little bit closer to it, and she falls in, and Bob doesn't?
cues.zh: Alice 离它稍微近一点，她掉了进去，而 Bob 没有？

cues.en: What happens? What happens is, she basically disappears.
cues.zh: 会发生什么？结果是，她基本上消失了。

cues.en: It seems that the other particle Bob is light being emitted as radiation from the Black hole,
cues.zh: 看起来另一个粒子 Bob 就是黑洞作为辐射发射出的光，

cues.en: and the Black hole will lose mass as a result.
cues.zh: 黑洞也因此损失质量。

cues.en: Black holes not only emit these very faint Hawking radiation, it evaporates over time.
cues.zh: 黑洞不仅会发出这种非常微弱的霍金辐射，而且它还会随时间蒸发。

cues.en: A physicist named Don Page, who is a very charming man,
cues.zh: 有位物理学家叫 Don Page，他是个非常有魅力的人，

cues.en: he's one of the people who just loves counting things.
cues.zh: 他就是那种特别喜欢数东西的人。

cues.en: One of the things he counted was essentially what amounts to the half-life of a black hole.
cues.zh: 他数过的东西之一，本质上就是黑洞的半衰期。

cues.en: That point at which the black hole has radiated away exactly half its mass, is called the Page time.
cues.zh: 黑洞正好辐射掉一半质量的那个时刻，叫做 Page 时间。

cues.en: It's kind of like the Mid-life Crisis for a black hole.
cues.zh: 这有点像黑洞的中年危机。

cues.en: It is relevant to the Firewalls debate.
cues.zh: 这与防火墙之争有关。

cues.en: Hawking radiation has some very troubling implications when it comes to information theory.
cues.zh: 就信息论而言，霍金辐射带来了一些非常令人不安的推论。

cues.en: and specifically what happens to information that falls into a Black hole.
cues.zh: 尤其是落入黑洞的信息会发生什么。

cues.en: This is where we get to the information paradox. Sean will talk more about this in depth as it pertains to Firewalls.
cues.zh: 这就引出了信息悖论。Sean 会结合防火墙更深入地讨论这一点。

cues.en: I'm just going to give you a brief overview now.
cues.zh: 我现在只给大家简要概述一下。

cues.en: It is very simple. We know that nothing can escape a Black hole.
cues.zh: 这很简单。我们知道，任何东西都无法逃出黑洞。

cues.en: So any information that falls into it, that Alice carries into it, should be lost.
cues.zh: 所以任何落入其中的信息，也就是 Alice 带进去的信息，都应该会丢失。

cues.en: There is a problem though, because there is a key precept in quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 但这里有个问题，因为量子力学中有一条关键原理，

cues.en: that says that information must be conserved.
cues.zh: 即信息必须守恒。

cues.en: It cannot be lost.
cues.zh: 信息不能丢失。

cues.en: Stephen Hawking decided that this was wrong,
cues.zh: Stephen Hawking 认定这是错的，

cues.en: and he put forward this very radical notion that information was lost.
cues.zh: 并提出一个非常激进的观点：信息会丢失。

cues.en: I think his famous quote is: "Not only does God play dice, but sometimes he confuses us by throwing them when they can't be seen. "
cues.zh: 我记得他的名言是：“上帝不仅掷骰子，有时还把骰子扔到看不见的地方，让我们困惑。”

cues.en: Kip Thorne, one of his colleagues, agreed with him.
cues.zh: 他的同事 Kip Thorne 也同意他的看法。

cues.en: John Preskill, another physicist, did not, and they made a very very famous bet in 1990s,
cues.zh: John Preskill，另一位物理学家，不这么认为，他们在1990年代打了一个非常著名的赌，

cues.en: where Hawking and Thorne basically said information is destroyed.
cues.zh: 霍金和索恩基本上是说信息会被摧毁。

cues.en: They said, OK technically you could say that it gets radiated out by Hawking radiation,
cues.zh: 他们说，好吧，严格来说你可以说信息会通过霍金辐射被辐射出去，

cues.en: but it's so scrambled that when the Black hole finally evaporates completely,
cues.zh: 但它被搅得太乱了，以至于当黑洞最终完全蒸发时，

cues.en: there is just no way we could retrieve that information.
cues.zh: 我们根本没办法找回那些信息。

cues.en: Basically, you are throwing a book into a bonfire, and it gets burnt up into complete ashes,
cues.zh: 基本上，就像你把一本书扔进篝火，它被烧成彻彻底底的灰烬，

cues.en: and then the ashes just integrate, and then there's nothing left.
cues.zh: 然后灰烬也消散了，就什么都不剩了。

cues.en: What do you do? That information is gone.
cues.zh: 那怎么办？那些信息已经没了。

cues.en: Preskill just didn't like this, so he basically took the opposite side of the bed.
cues.zh: Preskill 就是不喜欢这个说法，所以他基本上站到了对立面。

cues.en: He said that information could be recovered in principle,
cues.zh: 他说，原则上信息是可以恢复的，

cues.en: but he felt that physicists would need to devise a theory of quantum gravity
cues.zh: 但他认为，物理学家需要先构建出一套量子引力理论

cues.en: to really understand the mechanism by which this could occur.
cues.zh: 才能真正理解这一过程发生的机制。

cues.en: We don't have a theory of quantum gravity yet, as I mentioned.
cues.zh: 正如我提到的，我们目前还没有量子引力理论。

cues.en: But Hawking did, in fact, concede the bet in July 2004.
cues.zh: 但 Hawking 确实在 2004 年 7 月认输了这场赌局。

cues.en: This was actually based on some work by string theorists, again Sean will talk bout it more in depth.
cues.zh: 这其实基于一些弦论学家的研究，Sean 之后会更深入地讲。

cues.en: It's called the holographic principle.
cues.zh: 它叫全息原理。

cues.en: They basically found a cheat.
cues.zh: 他们基本上找到了一个作弊方法。

cues.en: The cheat is, as long as Alice and Bob can see two different things or have their own little bits of information,
cues.zh: 这个作弊方法是：只要 Alice 和 Bob 能看到两个不同的东西，或者各自掌握一点信息，

cues.en: as long as they don't communicate with each other, it's OK.
cues.zh: 只要他们彼此不通信，就没问题。

cues.en: Also, the information gets encoded not necessarily in the Black hole itself, but along the event horizon.
cues.zh: 另外，信息不一定编码在黑洞本身，而是沿着事件视界编码。

cues.en: It's a question of volume, so 3D becomes 2D.
cues.zh: 这是体积的问题，所以3D变成了2D。

cues.en: and that's a little trick they used mathematically to show that it was possible for information to be conserved.
cues.zh: 这是他们在数学上耍的一个小把戏，用来证明信息有可能守恒。

cues.en: What happened was Hawking presented Preskill with the eighth edition of Total Baseball: the ultimate baseball Encyclopaedia, "from which information can be retrieved at will".
cues.zh: 事情是这样的：霍金把《Total Baseball》第八版送给了普雷斯基尔——那是终极棒球百科全书，“从中可以随意取回信息”。

cues.en: And it was a big deal. Preskill was very happy.
cues.zh: 这可是件大事。普雷斯基尔非常高兴。

cues.en: But Kip Thorne refused to concede.
cues.zh: 但基普·索恩拒绝认输。

cues.en: He basically said: no there's more to the story. I don't think we have it.
cues.zh: 他基本上是在说：不，事情还没完。我不认为我们已经掌握了全部。

cues.en: It turns out that Thorne may have been correct not to concede,
cues.zh: 事实证明，Thorne 没有认输可能是对的，

cues.en: because today we have a new paradox, and that is Black hole Firewalls.
cues.zh: 因为今天我们有了一个新悖论，那就是黑洞火墙。

cues.en: This is something, again a paper that Joe Polchinski, a string theorist in Santa Barbara and Don Marolf
cues.zh: 这又是一篇论文，作者是圣巴巴拉的弦理论家 Joe Polchinski 和 Don Marolf，

cues.en: and a couple of their students came up with in the summer of 2012.
cues.zh: 以及他们的几个学生在 2012 年夏天提出的。

cues.en: They were playing around with the information paradox,
cues.zh: 他们当时在琢磨信息悖论，

cues.en: and Joe decided that he was going to try a little fun thought experiment,
cues.zh: Joe 决定尝试一个有趣的小思想实验，

cues.en: kind of run Hawking's thought experiments and a lot of thought processes backwards,
cues.zh: 有点像把 Hawking 的思想实验和许多思考过程倒着推一遍，

cues.en: just as a way to double-check, and make sure his logic was good.
cues.zh: 只是为了复核一下，确认自己的逻辑没问题。

cues.en: What he discovered was, there was an anomaly.
cues.zh: 他发现了一个反常现象。

cues.en: It was basically a logic problem that physicist Raphael Bousso calls it "the Menu from Hell".
cues.zh: 这本质上是一个逻辑问题，物理学家 Raphael Bousso 称之为“地狱菜单”。

cues.en: What it basically says is that, there are three fundamental precepts
cues.zh: 它基本上是说，有三条基本原理

cues.en: that physicists know and love and hold dear.
cues.zh: 是物理学家熟知、喜爱并珍视的。

cues.en: And what Polchinski at all found was that all of those three things cannot all be true.
cues.zh: 而 Polchinski 等人发现的是，这三件事不可能同时成立。

cues.en: They simply can't. You've got to pick one to give up.
cues.zh: 它们就是不能。你必须放弃其中一个。

cues.en: One of those, which we already talked about, is "no drama". It's the equivalence principle,
cues.zh: 其中之一我们已经谈过，就是“无戏剧性”。它是等效原理，

cues.en: the fact that Alice notices nothing unusual as she crosses the event horizon.
cues.zh: 即 Alice 穿过事件视界时没有注意到任何异常。

cues.en: We would really like to hang onto that,
cues.zh: 我们真的很想保留这一点，

cues.en: for reasons again which you will hear more of.
cues.zh: 原因后面你们还会听到更多。

cues.en: The second one is that we want information to be conserved.
cues.zh: 第二点是，我们希望信息守恒。

cues.en: We really want it to be conserved; it's a fundamental principle of quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 我们确实希望信息守恒；这是量子力学的一条基本原理，

cues.en: and if that's wrong, all hell breaks loose in quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 如果这错了，量子力学就会乱套。

cues.en: The third thing is Locality, which is a little harder to describe,
cues.zh: 第三点是定域性，这有点难描述，

cues.en: but essentially, if you picture dropping a pebble in a pond, and it starts to ripple and it ripples outwards.
cues.zh: 但本质上，如果你想象往池塘里扔一颗石子，它开始泛起涟漪并向外扩散。

cues.en: The basic activity of dropping a pebble happens locally;
cues.zh: 扔下一颗卵石的基本动作是局部发生的；

cues.en: it doesn't happen everywhere at once, and that it spreads out.
cues.zh: 它不会同时在所有地方发生，而是向外扩散。

cues.en: That's locality.
cues.zh: 这就是局域性。

cues.en: Locality is actually one of the foundations of physics.
cues.zh: 局域性其实是物理学的基础之一。

cues.en: It's really really central. So central that it's hard to think of...certainly classical physics without it.
cues.zh: 它非常非常核心。核心到很难想象……至少经典物理学离了它就无法想象。

cues.en: Which one has to go? Nobody wants to give away any of these.
cues.zh: 那哪一个必须放弃？这些谁也不愿舍弃。

cues.en: I actually had the privilege of going to a Stanford workshop shortly after the Firewalls paper was published,
cues.zh: 其实在 Firewalls 论文发表后不久，我有幸去了斯坦福的一个研讨会，

cues.en: the first Firewalls paper,
cues.zh: 第一篇 Firewalls 论文，

cues.en: and watching them fight it out.
cues.zh: 看他们争得不可开交。

cues.en: It was fascinating to watch, because nobody knew the answer.
cues.zh: 那场讨论很有意思，因为没人知道答案。

cues.en: They still don't; they are still arguing about it.
cues.zh: 他们现在仍然不知道；还在为此争论。

cues.en: But the most obvious, easiest solution to it is to get rid of "no drama",
cues.zh: 但它最明显、最简单的解决办法，就是抛弃“no drama”，

cues.en: and when you sacrifice "no drama", you get a Firewall,
cues.zh: 而一旦牺牲“no drama”，你就会得到一道防火墙，

cues.en: a wall of radiation at the event horizon,
cues.zh: 一道位于事件视界的辐射墙，

cues.en: and poor Alice gets burnt alive.
cues.zh: 可怜的 Alice 就会被活活烧死。

cues.en: I personally would like to save poor Alice; I don't know how we are going to do that.
cues.zh: 我个人很想救可怜的 Alice；但我不知道我们该怎么做。

cues.en: I am hoping that my husband, Sean Carroll, can come up here, and take you through the next stage of the talk.
cues.zh: 我希望我丈夫 Sean Carroll 能上来，带你们进入演讲的下一阶段。

cues.en: Hopefully he can find a way to save Alice.
cues.zh: 希望他能找到办法救 Alice。

cues.en: [APPLAUSE]
cues.zh: [掌声]

cues.en: SEAN: Yes, we'll see what we can do.
cues.zh: SEAN：对，我们会看看能做什么。

cues.en: The answer is "no", we will not be able to save Alice.
cues.zh: 答案是“不能”，我们救不了 Alice。

cues.en: This is not - sometimes I go around giving talks about the discovery of the Higgs boson,
cues.zh: 这不是——有时我会四处做关于发现希格斯玻色子的演讲，

cues.en: and it's a wonderful privilege to do that, because there is a climax.
cues.zh: 能做这件事是极大的荣幸，因为有一个高潮。

cues.en: We discovered the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 我们发现了希格斯玻色子。

cues.en: It is a triumphant event.
cues.zh: 这是一个凯旋般的事件。

cues.en: There will be no climactic triumphal event at this talk.
cues.zh: 这次演讲不会有高潮式的凯旋时刻。

cues.en: This is going to say "hey look, there is this puzzle. I don't know what the answer is.
cues.zh: 它会说：“嘿，看，有这么个谜题。我不知道答案是什么。

cues.en: Maybe someone in the audience can help us out."
cues.zh: 也许观众里有人能帮我们解答。”

cues.en: It all comes, as Jennifer said, from taking the idea of a Black hole, which is well established,
cues.zh: 正如 Jennifer 所说，这一切都源于采用黑洞这个成熟的概念，

cues.en: and which we understand in the context of classical mechanics, and applying quantum mechanics too.
cues.zh: 我们在经典力学框架下理解它，同时也把量子力学应用上去。

cues.en: Classical mechanics is what was handed down to us from Newton through Maxwell and Einstein.
cues.zh: 经典力学是从 Newton 经 Maxwell 到 Einstein 一路传下来的。

cues.en: It's the idea that you have a state of affairs in the universe,
cues.zh: 这个想法是，宇宙中存在某种状态，

cues.en: and it evolves predictably through time.
cues.zh: 并且它随时间可预测地演化。

cues.en: Also, what you see is what there is.
cues.zh: 另外，你看到的就是存在的东西。

cues.en: In classical mechanics, there just IS something and you can observe it.
cues.zh: 在经典力学中，就是存在某物，而且你能观测到它。

cues.en: In quantum mechanics, that's not quite the case.
cues.zh: 在量子力学中，情况就不太一样了。

cues.en: So here is your one minute introduction to quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 那么，这就是你的一分钟量子力学入门。

cues.en: What you can observe is much less than what actually exists.
cues.zh: 你能观测到的，远少于实际存在的东西。

cues.en: That's really the essence of quantum mechanics and why it's difficult to understand,
cues.zh: 这正是量子力学的本质，也是它难以理解的原因，

cues.en: because nobody likes this. Nobody likes the fact that some fundamental deep facet of physics
cues.zh: 因为没人喜欢这样。没人喜欢物理学某个根本而深层的方面

cues.en: is being expressed in terms of what human beings can observe.
cues.zh: 竟然要用人类能观测到什么来表达。

cues.en: That can't be right.
cues.zh: 这不可能是对的。

cues.en: And this is called the ""measurement problem" of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 这就是量子力学中的“测量问题”。

cues.en: Surely we don't understand quantum mechanics well enough if we are reduced to making statements like this.
cues.zh: 如果我们只能说出这样的话，那说明我们对量子力学的理解肯定还不够。

cues.en: And it turns out that we do understand quantum mechanics better than we used to.
cues.zh: 而事实证明，我们对量子力学的理解确实比以前更透彻了。

cues.en: We know a little bit more about what qualifies as an observer and a measurement.
cues.zh: 对于什么才算观察者、什么才算测量，我们了解得更多了一些。

cues.en: We still don't know everything; we still don't have a complete picture that everyone agrees on,
cues.zh: 我们仍然不是什么都懂；关于基本的量子力学实在，我们仍然没有一个所有人都认同的完整图景，

cues.en: on the basic quantum mechanical reality.
cues.zh: 关于基本的量子力学实在。

cues.en: But we know how it works, in practice. How it works is, certain kinds of observations that you can make.
cues.zh: 但实践中我们知道它如何运作。运作方式是，你能进行某些类型的观测。

cues.en: They return results that we can predict - the probability of getting a result.
cues.zh: 它们会返回我们能预测的结果——得到某个结果的概率。

cues.en: But when you are not making those observations, when you are not looking at this system,
cues.zh: 但当你没有进行那些观测时，当你没有观察这个系统时，

cues.en: all of the different possibilities can simultaneously be there.
cues.zh: 所有不同的可能性可以同时存在。

cues.en: So here is a classical example - Jennifer mentioned: The Schrodinger's cat.
cues.zh: 所以这里有个经典例子——Jennifer 提到过：薛定谔的猫。

cues.en: One of a long line of experiments, that are among the most violent thought experiments that physicists like to talk about,
cues.zh: 这是一系列实验中的一个，属于物理学家最喜欢谈论的那类最暴力的思想实验，

cues.en: where we kill small helpless animals.
cues.zh: 在这些实验里，我们会杀死弱小无助的动物。

cues.en: In this case, well we kill half of the animal.
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，我们会杀死动物的一半。

cues.en: We kill the animal at some branch of the wave function of the universe.
cues.zh: 我们会在宇宙波函数的某个分支上杀死这只动物。

cues.en: In this case, you have a cat; it's in a box,
cues.zh: 这个例子里，你有一只猫，它在一个盒子里，

cues.en: and what you want to do, is that you want to take advantage of the fact that in quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 你想做的是，利用量子力学中的这样一个事实：

cues.en: systems can be in superpositions of different classical possibilities.
cues.zh: 系统可以处于不同经典可能性的叠加态。

cues.en: So in the box, you hook up a Geiger counter to a radioactive source, a hammer that can fall,
cues.zh: 在箱子里，你把盖革计数器接到放射源上，还有一个能落下的锤子，

cues.en: and break a vile that is filled with poisoned gas.
cues.zh: 去打破一个装满毒气的小瓶。

cues.en: It has to be a Geiger counter or something else that is sensitive to a quantum mechanical event,
cues.zh: 它必须是盖革计数器，或者其他对量子力学事件敏感的装置，

cues.en: like the decay of an atom.
cues.zh: 比如原子的衰变。

cues.en: So there's something fundamentally quantum mechanical; it happens with a certain probablity,
cues.zh: 所以这里有某种本质上是量子力学的东西；它以一定的概率发生，

cues.en: and you wait until that probability adds up to 50%.
cues.zh: 然后你一直等到这个概率累积到 50%。

cues.en: Then according to the rules of quantum mechanics, Schrodinger points out that, in this box,
cues.zh: 然后根据量子力学规则，薛定谔指出，在这个盒子里，

cues.en: there is no such thing as an alive cat or a dead cat.
cues.zh: 并不存在所谓的活猫或死猫。

cues.en: In this box, the reality of the situation is that there is a superposition of an alive cat and a dead cat.
cues.zh: 在这个盒子里，实际情况是，活猫和死猫处于叠加态。

cues.en: We are used to, in classical mechanics, having boxes that we don't know what's in there.
cues.zh: 在经典力学中，我们习惯于面对不知道里面有什么的盒子。

cues.en: You might say that there is a 50-50 chance that the cat is alive or dead.
cues.zh: 你可能会说，猫是死是活各有一半的概率。

cues.en: But in that way of talking, there is a reality, you just don't know what it is.
cues.zh: 但按那种说法，确实存在一个现实，只是你不知道它是什么。

cues.en: it is a matter of our ignorance.
cues.zh: 这只是我们无知的问题。

cues.en: In quantum mechanics, it's not just a matter of our ignorance.
cues.zh: 在量子力学中，这不仅仅是我们无知的问题。

cues.en: The truth of what's inside the box, is that it is both an alive cat and a dead cat,
cues.zh: 盒子里的真相是：它既是活猫，也是死猫，

cues.en: a superposition of both possibilities.
cues.zh: 是两种可能性的叠加态。

cues.en: And again, these days we know more about quantum mechanics than Schrodinger did,
cues.zh: 再说，如今我们对量子力学的了解已经超过薛定谔当年，

cues.en: so we know that, you don'y need to open the box to create either the alive cat or the dead cat.
cues.zh: 所以我们知道，你不需要打开盒子，就能得到活猫或死猫中的一种。

cues.en: There is an effective observation being made all the time by the air in the box, by the light in the box,
cues.zh: 盒子里的空气、盒子里的光，

cues.en: by the cat walking around and so forth.
cues.zh: 还有走来走去的猫等等，始终都在进行有效观测。

cues.en: Long before you open the box, the split has already happened.
cues.zh: 远在你打开盒子之前，分裂就已经发生了。

cues.en: But the classical explanation of this thought experiment is that, before you open the box,
cues.zh: 但这个思想实验的经典解释是，在你打开盒子之前，

cues.en: there is a superposition of a live cat and a dead cat.
cues.zh: 活猫和死猫处于叠加态。

cues.en: When you open it and observe, you only ever see either the cat alive, or the cat dead.
cues.zh: 当你打开盒子观测时，你只会看到猫要么活着，要么死了。

cues.en: You never see a superposition of both possibilities, even though that's what quantum mechanics says is there
cues.zh: 你永远不会看到两种可能性叠加在一起，尽管量子力学说它就在那里

cues.en: when you are not looking.
cues.zh: 在你没有观测的时候。

cues.en: And that's the fundamental mystery of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 这就是量子力学最根本的谜团。

cues.en: The way that when you are not looking at something, it's in a superposition of all these different possibilities.
cues.zh: 当你没有观测某物时，它处于所有这些不同可能性的叠加态。

cues.en: That leads to something that's very important for the Firewall story, something called entanglement.
cues.zh: 这就引出了对 Firewall 故事至关重要的东西——所谓的纠缠。

cues.en: This is not a picture of entanglement. This is just an excuse to put a cute cat on the slide.
cues.zh: 这不是纠缠的图片。这只是找个借口，在幻灯片上放只可爱的猫。

cues.en: Entanglement is the idea that in quantum mechanics, the way that we describe the world is not piece by piece.
cues.zh: 纠缠指的是，在量子力学中，我们描述世界的方式不是一块一块地。

cues.en: it's all at once.
cues.zh: 而是一次性整体描述。

cues.en: So in classical mechanics, let's say you have two boxes, and you can't see inside,
cues.zh: 所以在经典力学中，假设你有两个盒子，你看不到里面，

cues.en: and you have a red ball and a blue ball.
cues.zh: 你有一个红球和一个蓝球。

cues.en: You know that there is one of each, and each one is inside a box, but you don't know which one is in which box.
cues.zh: 你知道每种各有一个，每个都在一个盒子里，但你不知道哪个在哪个盒子里。

cues.en: Then you would say that there are two possibilities: either that the blue ball is in box one,
cues.zh: 那么你会说有两种可能性：要么蓝球在盒子里一，

cues.en: and the red one is in box two;
cues.zh: 红球在盒子里二；

cues.en: OR the red one is in box one, and the blue one is in box two.
cues.zh: 要么红球在盒子里一，蓝球在盒子里二。

cues.en: One of those possibilities is true in classical mechanics, whether or not you know it.
cues.zh: 在经典力学中，其中一种可能性为真，无论你是否知道。

cues.en: In quantum mechanics, inside the box you can have any superposition of maybe it's the red ball, maybe it's the blue ball.
cues.zh: 在量子力学中，盒子内部可以处于任意叠加态，也许是红球，也许是蓝球。

cues.en: So in quantum mechanics, there can be entanglement.
cues.zh: 所以在量子力学中，可以存在纠缠。

cues.en: Not only that it can be true that in one box, a certain chance that the ball is blue,
cues.zh: 不仅如此，在一个盒子里，球有一定概率是蓝色，

cues.en: but it can be the case that in the other box, whichever option is real depends on what's going on in the first box.
cues.zh: 但也可能另一个盒子里实际是哪种情况，取决于第一个盒子里发生什么。

cues.en: If you open just one box, it might be 50-50, the ball is red, or the ball is blue.
cues.zh: 如果你只打开一个盒子，可能是五五开，球是红色，或者球是蓝色。

cues.en: If you open the other box, likewise, 50-50, red versus blue.
cues.zh: 如果你打开另一个盒子，同样五五开，红对蓝。

cues.en: But if you open the first box and the ball is red, then you know with 100% certainty the other box is blue.
cues.zh: 但如果你打开第一个盒子，球是红色，那你就百分百确定另一个盒子是蓝色。

cues.en: That is quantum entanglement, and if you want to be a little more of a respectable particle physicist,
cues.zh: 这就是量子纠缠。如果你想显得更像个正经的粒子物理学家，

cues.en: you can think of particles spinning or moving in certain directions,
cues.zh: 可以把粒子想成在朝某些方向自旋或运动，

cues.en: rather than balls being red or blue.
cues.zh: 而不是把球分成红色或蓝色。

cues.en: But it's the same overall point,
cues.zh: 但总体要点是一样的，

cues.en: that quantum mechanics does not say there is a state of this box, and a state of this box.
cues.zh: 量子力学并不是说，这个盒子有一个状态，那个盒子有一个状态。

cues.en: It says there is the state of the world.
cues.zh: 它说的是，存在一个世界的状态。

cues.en: In this case, the world is either, red over here and blue over there,
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，世界要么是这边红、那边蓝，

cues.en: OR blue over here, red over there.
cues.zh: 要么这边蓝、那边红。

cues.en: So this little picture is supposed to show not two balls in each box,
cues.zh: 所以这张小图要展示的不是每个盒子里有两个球，

cues.en: but the balls are in superposition of red and blue, that it is entangled between those two boxes.
cues.zh: 而是这些球处于红色和蓝色的叠加态，而且两个盒子之间是纠缠的。

cues.en: This is another mystery of quantum mechanics. Forget about the measurement stuff.
cues.zh: 这是量子力学的另一个谜团。先不提测量那套东西。

cues.en: The fact that things that are separated from each other can nevertheless be entangled with each other
cues.zh: 彼此分离的东西仍然可以相互纠缠，

cues.en: bugs us also.
cues.zh: 这一点也让我们困扰。

cues.en: It certainly bugged Einstein.
cues.zh: 它显然也困扰了爱因斯坦。

cues.en: He wrote a paper in 1935 with his friends Podolsky and Rosen.
cues.zh: 1935年，他和朋友Podolsky和Rosen写了一篇论文。

cues.en: He came up with one of the paradoxes that Jennifer mentioned.
cues.zh: 他提出了Jennifer提到过的其中一个悖论。

cues.en: The paradox, the EPR paradox - The Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen, says,
cues.zh: 这个悖论，EPR悖论，也就是Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen悖论，说的是，

cues.en: look, this entanglement between two different particles,
cues.zh: 看，两个不同粒子之间的这种纠缠，

cues.en: let's say a particle spinning clockwise, and a particle spinning counter-clockwise, or something like that,
cues.zh: 比如说一个粒子顺时针自旋，另一个粒子逆时针自旋，诸如此类，

cues.en: or a ball being red or blue.
cues.zh: 或者一个球是红色或蓝色。

cues.en: You see, you have one particle over here that's in one state;
cues.zh: 你看，这边有一个粒子处于一种状态；

cues.en: another particle in another state, and they are entangled with each other.
cues.zh: 另一个粒子处于另一种状态，而且它们彼此纠缠。

cues.en: That entanglement can persist no matter how far apart the particles are.
cues.zh: 这种纠缠无论粒子相隔多远都能保持。

cues.en: You can have one particle that is entangled with the other,
cues.zh: 可以有一个粒子与另一个粒子纠缠，

cues.en: even though they can be separated by hundreds of thousands of light years.
cues.zh: 哪怕它们相隔几十万光年。

cues.en: They are on separate sides of a galaxy.
cues.zh: 它们位于星系的两端。

cues.en: This is not a picture of our galaxy, by the way, we don't have any pictures of our galaxy.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这不是我们银河系的照片，我们根本没有银河系的照片。

cues.en: This is the Andromeda galaxy.
cues.zh: 这是仙女座星系。

cues.en: But the principle is the same.
cues.zh: 但原理是一样的。

cues.en: In fact, we have done experiments like this,
cues.zh: 事实上，我们做过这样的实验，

cues.en: where two particles are entangled; they are separated by kilometres.
cues.zh: 两个粒子相互纠缠，彼此相隔数公里。

cues.en: They are not separated by hundreds of thousands of light years.
cues.zh: 它们并没有相隔几十万光年。

cues.en: But still kilometres are pretty good.
cues.zh: 但以公里计也已经很不错了。

cues.en: According to the rules of quantum mechanics, if you observe this one and then see the ball if blue,
cues.zh: 根据量子力学规则，如果你观测这一个，发现球是蓝色的，

cues.en: you instantly know that the ball on the other side of the galaxy is red.
cues.zh: 你就能立刻知道银河系另一端的球是红色的。

cues.en: So this bugs us, because as Einstein pointed out,
cues.zh: 所以这让我们很困扰，因为正如爱因斯坦指出的，

cues.en: nothing can travel faster than the speed of light.
cues.zh: 没有什么能超过光速。

cues.en: But the reality of which ball is in the box seems to be changing instantaneously all over the universe.
cues.zh: 但盒子里究竟是哪个球，这个现实似乎会在全宇宙中瞬间改变。

cues.en: That bothers us a great deal.
cues.zh: 这让我们很在意。

cues.en: However, it turns out that this kind of instantaneous change is relatively harmless.
cues.zh: 不过，这种瞬时变化其实相对无害。

cues.en: You can't use this to talk to anybody, on the other side of the galaxy.
cues.zh: 你没法用它和银河系另一边的任何人通信。

cues.en: If you think about it, your friend over here, what do they know before you open the box?
cues.zh: 想想看，你这边这位朋友，在你打开盒子之前，他知道什么？

cues.en: They know that if they open their box, the ball could be red or it could be blue.
cues.zh: 他知道，如果他打开自己的盒子，球可能是红色，也可能是蓝色。

cues.en: So you open your box, and your find that the ball is red.
cues.zh: 于是你打开盒子，发现球是红色的。

cues.en: You know that when they open the box, it is going to be blue,
cues.zh: 你知道，当他们打开盒子时，它会是蓝色的，

cues.en: with 100% probability.
But they don't know that. They open the box and it is blue,
cues.zh: 但他们并不知道这一点。他们打开盒子，发现它是蓝色的，

cues.en: and they go:"Well, that was one of the chances"
cues.zh: 然后说：“好吧，那只是其中一种可能。”

cues.en: No information has travelled.
cues.zh: 没有任何信息被传递。

cues.en: You cannot send a telegraph using this kind of entanglement.
cues.zh: 你没法用这种纠缠来发电报。

cues.en: So quantum mechanics manages to be non-local in a very subtle way.
cues.zh: 所以量子力学以一种非常微妙的方式实现了非局域性。

cues.en: It bugged Einstein, but again, all he could do was say :"Look, this sounds weird"
cues.zh: 这一点让爱因斯坦很困扰，但他能说的也只是：“看，这听起来很奇怪。”

cues.en: and the rest of the community said: "Yes, that does sound weird, but it's true. "
cues.zh: 而学界其他人说：“是的，这确实听起来很奇怪，但它是真的。”

cues.en: You'll do the experiment and it's true. this is actually how nature works.
cues.zh: 你去做实验，结果是真的。大自然实际上就是这样运作的。

cues.en: The reason why I am going to such a great length talking about this here, is because
cues.zh: 我在这里花这么大篇幅讲这个，是因为

cues.en: the particles that are emitted by Black holes are entangled in a very very specific way.
cues.zh: 黑洞发射出的粒子，以一种非常非常特殊的方式纠缠在一起。

cues.en: Jennifer showed you some nice pictures of Black holes at one moment in time.
cues.zh: Jennifer 给你们看过一些黑洞在某一时刻的漂亮图片。

cues.en: The Black holes sitting there in space, just a black sphere with fun radiation and people falling onto it.
cues.zh: 黑洞悬在太空里，就是一个黑色球体，有有趣的辐射，还有人往里掉。

cues.en: I am the hard core quantitate of science, so I drew a little picture, in power point.
cues.zh: 我是科学界的硬核定量派，所以我在 PowerPoint 里画了张小图。

cues.en: This is a space-time diagram of a Black hole.
cues.zh: 这是一张黑洞的时空图。

cues.en: The hole itself, the two-dimensional surface enclosing a three-dimensional volume
cues.zh: 这个洞本身，即包围三维体积的二维曲面，

cues.en: is here portrayed as a just a one-dimensional circle enclosing a two dimensional disc.
cues.zh: 在这里被画成一个一维的圆，围住一个二维的圆盘。

cues.en: This circle is the black hole at one moment in time.
cues.zh: 这个圆是某一时刻的黑洞。

cues.en: And the vertical axis is time evolving.
cues.zh: 而竖直轴是时间演化。

cues.en: The black hole is just sitting there, so nothing is actually happening in this picture,
cues.zh: 黑洞只是静止在那里，所以这张图里其实什么都没发生，

cues.en: but we are going to make it a little bit more active in just a second.
cues.zh: 不过我们马上会让它稍微活跃一点。

cues.en: And inside you see the singularity, and the event horizon defines the boundary of a Black hole.
cues.zh: 而在内部你会看到奇点，事件视界则定义了黑洞的边界。

cues.en: For those of you that have been reading ahead, outside of class,
cues.zh: 那些在课外提前预习过的同学，

cues.en: you will know that outside the event horizon time goes vertically, but inside, time heads into the singularity.
cues.zh: 会知道在事件视界之外，时间是竖直向走的，但在内部，时间指向奇点。

cues.en: Once you are inside the event horizon,
cues.zh: 一旦你进入事件视界之内，

cues.en: moving towards the singularity is precisely the same as moving forward in time.
cues.zh: 朝奇点移动，就完全等同于在时间中向前走。

cues.en: You can no more avoid heading towards the singularity than you can avoid heading tomorrow.
cues.zh: 你无法避免朝奇点前进，就像你无法避免走向明天一样。

cues.en: That is why the singularity is so inevitable.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么奇点如此不可避免。

cues.en: Now what Stephen Hawking said is, out of this classical Black hole will come radiation,
cues.zh: 现在，Stephen Hawking 说的是，辐射会从这个经典黑洞中向外发出，

cues.en: and one way to think about that is, near the event horizon, according to the "no drama" principle,
cues.zh: 一种理解方式是，在事件视界附近，根据“无戏剧”原则，

cues.en: the principle of equivalence that Jennifer talked about,
cues.zh: Jennifer 谈到的等价原则，

cues.en: you are in, what physicists call, the vacuum state.
cues.zh: 你正处于物理学家所说的真空态。

cues.en: You are in empty space, there is nothing there.
cues.zh: 你身处一片虚空，那里什么都没有。

cues.en: You can pass through the event horizon with a little detector, looking for particles,
cues.zh: 你可以带着一个小探测器穿过事件视界，寻找粒子，

cues.en: you don't see anything special; there's no sign posts, no "no escape after you meet this point"
cues.zh: 你看不出任何特别之处；没有路标，也没有“到这里就再也逃不出去”的提示。

cues.en: or anything like that.
cues.zh: 或者诸如此类的东西。

cues.en: But it's an empty space that obeys the rules of quantum mechanics
cues.zh: 但这片真空遵循量子力学的规则

cues.en: and in quantum mechanics, even empty space is kind of interesting.
cues.zh: 而在量子力学里，连真空都挺有意思。

cues.en: Empty space is actually a superposition of different ways that particles could be coming in and out of existence.
cues.zh: 真空其实是粒子以各种方式不断产生又湮灭的叠加态。

cues.en: Now, here in this room, space is empty, and space-time is fairly flat,
cues.zh: 现在，在这个房间里，空间是空的，时空相当平坦，

cues.en: because gravitational field is not that strong.
cues.zh: 因为引力场没那么强。

cues.en: if you look at empty space, you truly don't see anything.
cues.zh: 如果你看真空，确实什么都看不到。

cues.en: but in the vicinity of a Black Hole, what Hawking points out,
cues.zh: 但在黑洞附近，霍金指出，

cues.en: is that the gravitational field of a Black hole can tear apart these virtual particles that are sitting in the quantum vacuum.
cues.zh: 黑洞的引力场会把这些位于量子真空中的虚粒子撕开。

cues.en: So you can have one particle, Alice, falling into the Black hole, and another particle Bob escaping into infinity.
cues.zh: 于是可以有一个粒子 Alice 落入黑洞，另一个粒子 Bob 逃逸到无穷远。

cues.en: So what was two particles sitting there quietly in empty space
cues.zh: 原本只是两个安静待在空无一物空间里的粒子

cues.en: becomes two real actual particles.
cues.zh: 变成了两个真实存在的粒子。

cues.en: That's very important; this one particle that goes out is what we call the Hawking radiation.
cues.zh: 这很重要；这个跑出去的粒子就是我们所说的霍金辐射。

cues.en: That's what we see evaporating away from the Black hole.
cues.zh: 这就是我们看到从黑洞中蒸发出去的东西。

cues.en: So it's important that whenever you make one Hawking particle, that escapes the Black hole,
cues.zh: 所以重要的是，每当你产生一个逃出黑洞的霍金粒子时，

cues.en: secretly, although you don't see it from out here, there is another particle that you also made
cues.zh: 隐秘的是，虽然你从外面看不到，你还产生了另一个粒子，

cues.en: that falls into the Black hole.
cues.zh: 它会落入黑洞。

cues.en: Given all the setup, you will not be surprised to hear that the two particles are entangled with each other.
cues.zh: 有了这些前提，听到这两个粒子彼此纠缠，你也不会感到意外。

cues.en: That makes sense, because these two particles are created essentially out of nothing,
cues.zh: 这说得通，因为这两个粒子本质上是从虚无中产生的，

cues.en: out of empty space.
cues.zh: 是从空无一物的空间中产生的。

cues.en: Empty space does not have any electric charge, does not have any spin. It doesn't have any energy.
cues.zh: 空无一物的空间没有电荷，没有自旋，也没有能量。

cues.en: It's empty space,
cues.zh: 它是空无一物的空间，

cues.en: But you've made particles out of it.
cues.zh: 但你从中制造出了粒子。

cues.en: Therefore the two particles that you pulled out of empty space
cues.zh: 因此，你从空无一物的空间中拉出的那两个粒子

cues.en: need to be equal but also opposite.
cues.zh: 必须相等，但彼此相反。

cues.en: If one of them has a positive electric charge, the other one has a negative electric charge.
cues.zh: 如果其中一个带正电荷，另一个就带负电荷。

cues.en: One of them is spinning clockwise; the other one is spinning counter-clockwise.
cues.zh: 其中一个顺时针自旋，另一个逆时针自旋。

cues.en: If one of them has a positive amount of energy, the other one has a negative amount of energy.
cues.zh: 如果其中一个具有正能量，另一个就具有负能量。

cues.en: And indeed, any particle that escapes to infinity, to the outside world has a positive amount of energy.
cues.zh: 而事实上，任何逃逸到无穷远、逃到外部世界的粒子都具有正能量。

cues.en: Therefore, as far as the outside observer is concerned,
cues.zh: 因此，对外部观察者而言，

cues.en: Alice, the in-falling particle, has a negative amount of energy.
cues.zh: Alice，这个落入黑洞的粒子，具有负能量。

cues.en: That's why the Black holes eventually shrink and lose their masses
cues.zh: 这就是黑洞最终会收缩并失去质量的原因

cues.en: because essentially, inside the Black hole,
cues.zh: 因为本质上，在黑洞内部，

cues.en: you see a constant drizzle of negative energy particles decreasing the mass of a Black hole.
cues.zh: 你会看到负能量粒子持续不断地滴落，减少黑洞的质量。

cues.en: These two particles, Alice and Bob, that are created by Hawking radiation,
cues.zh: Alice 和 Bob 这两个由霍金辐射产生的粒子，

cues.en: are entangled with each other.
cues.zh: 彼此纠缠在一起。

cues.en: if this one is spinning one way, this one is spinning the other way.
cues.zh: 如果这个朝一个方向自旋，那个就朝另一个方向自旋。

cues.en: Empty space separated into sets of particles, will necessarily give you particles that are always entangled.
cues.zh: 真空被分成一组组粒子时，必然会产生始终相互纠缠的粒子。

cues.en: That's a consequence of the "no drama" principle.
cues.zh: 这是“无戏剧”原理的一个结果。

cues.en: however, we want more than that.
cues.zh: 然而，我们想要的还不止这些。

cues.en: We want the information, having which we made the Black hole, to eventually escape
cues.zh: 我们希望，当初制造黑洞时所拥有的信息最终能逃逸出来

cues.en: Once the whole Black hole has evaporated, we want to know exactly what it was made of.
cues.zh: 一旦整个黑洞蒸发完毕，我们想确切知道它是由什么构成的。

cues.en: We know that you have two particles entangled;
cues.zh: 我们知道有两个粒子处于纠缠态；

cues.en: we know that all the particles coming out are supposed to tell us what went in in the first place.
cues.zh: 我们知道，所有出来的粒子本应告诉我们最初进去的是什么。

cues.en: But that's a puzzle, because Bob is entangled with Alice,
cues.zh: 但这就成了个谜，因为 Bob 和 Alice 纠缠在一起，

cues.en: and what that means is that some of Bob's information is being left behind in the Black hole.
cues.zh: 这意味着 Bob 的一部分信息被留在了黑洞里。

cues.en: When Bob leaves, Bob is entangled, and we are not exactly sure how; therefore the information is not yet getting out.
cues.zh: 当 Bob 离开时，Bob 处于纠缠态，而我们并不确切知道是怎么纠缠的；因此信息还没有出来。

cues.en: What you'd say to yourself, if you are trying to make sense of this,
cues.zh: 如果你试图理解这件事，你会对自己说，

cues.en: if you are a physicist who believes that Black holes evaporate,
cues.zh: 如果你是一位相信黑洞会蒸发的物理学家，

cues.en: but also believes that information is conserved, is that:
cues.zh: 但也相信信息守恒，那么你会说：

cues.en: That's OK, because later there is another particle named Carrie, and Bob will just be entangled with Carrie,
cues.zh: 没关系，因为之后会有另一个名叫 Carrie 的粒子，而 Bob 只会与 Carrie 纠缠，

cues.en: in exactly the same way that he was entangled with Alice.
cues.zh: 方式和他与 Alice 纠缠时完全相同。

cues.en: So Bob is spinning clockwise; both Alice and Carrie are spinning counter-clockwise,
cues.zh: 所以 Bob 是顺时针旋转；Alice 和 Carrie 都是逆时针旋转，

cues.en: and vice versa.
cues.zh: 反之亦然。

cues.en: So maybe that's how the information gets out. This early radiation Bob, is entangled with the late radiation Carrie.
cues.zh: 所以信息也许就是这么出来的。这个早期辐射 Bob，与晚期辐射 Carrie 纠缠在一起。

cues.en: Then of course, Carrie herself, if she is a virtual particle that was torn out of the quantum vacuum,
cues.zh: 当然，Carrie 自己如果是从量子真空中被撕出来的虚粒子，

cues.en: she'll also be entangled with Dave, but Dave is just not going to be important to our story.
cues.zh: 她也会和 Dave 纠缠，但 Dave 在我们的故事里并不重要。

cues.en: Sorry Dave.
cues.zh: 抱歉，Dave。

cues.en: Here is what we are trying to say.
cues.zh: 我们想说的是。

cues.en: We are trying to say that Bob started life entangled with Alice
cues.zh: 我们想说的是，Bob 一开始和 Alice 纠缠在一起，

cues.en: and eventually is entangled with Carrie.
cues.zh: 最终又和 Carrie 纠缠在一起。

cues.en: That's the only way that information can get out of Black holes, if there is "no drama" at the event horizon.
cues.zh: 那是信息能离开黑洞的唯一方式，前提是事件视界处“没有戏剧性”。

cues.en: The problem is, that cannot happen.
cues.zh: 问题是，那不可能发生。

cues.en: Quantum entanglement does not work that way.
cues.zh: 量子纠缠不是这样运作的。

cues.en: Quantum entanglement does not let you mess around.
cues.zh: 量子纠缠不允许你乱来。

cues.en: Sorry
cues.zh: 抱歉

cues.en: In fact, literally, the phrase this goes by is the "Monogamy of entanglement"
cues.zh: 事实上，这个说法的字面名称就是“纠缠的单配性”

cues.en: If you are a particle Bob, and you are maximumly entangled with another particle Alice,
cues.zh: 如果你是一个粒子Bob，并且与另一个粒子Alice处于最大纠缠，

cues.en: (there is Alice and there is Bob),
cues.zh: （有Alice，也有Bob），

cues.en: you cannot possibly be entangled even a little bit with another particle called Carrie.
cues.zh: 你就不可能和另一个叫Carrie的粒子有哪怕一点点纠缠。

cues.en: The rules of quantum entanglement are more strict than the rules of "free love" in the 60s,
cues.zh: 量子纠缠的规则比 60 年代“自由恋爱”的规则更严格，

cues.en: when this was first discusses.
cues.zh: 这是最初讨论它的时候。

cues.en: I got this slide, this picture, from John Preskill, who Jennifer already mentioned,
cues.zh: 这张幻灯片、这张图，是 John Preskill 给我的，Jennifer 刚才提到过他，

cues.en: a colleague of mine in CalTech.
cues.zh: 他是我在 CalTech 的同事。

cues.en: John got in trouble for showing this slide, because it says on the top: Monogamy is frustrating!
cues.zh: John 因为展示这张幻灯片惹了麻烦，因为顶部写着：一夫一妻制真让人沮丧！

cues.en: As if poor bob is frustrated because he is stuck in this relationship with Alice,
cues.zh: 就好像可怜的 Bob 因为被困在和 Alice 的关系里而沮丧，

cues.en: and he can't get together with Carrie.
cues.zh: 而且他不能和 Carrie 在一起。

cues.en: So John started changing the labels and he made it Becky over here,
cues.zh: 于是 John 开始改标签，把这边标成了 Becky，

cues.en: who is entangled with Adam,
cues.zh: 她与 Adam 纠缠，

cues.en: and cannot be entangled with Charlie.
cues.zh: 且不能与 Charlie 纠缠。

cues.en: Then he got into trouble for that too, because people were saying:
cues.zh: 然后他也因此惹上了麻烦，因为人们说：

cues.en: "What are you saying about Beckie's morals anyway? Beckie is just sleeping around? Come on. "
cues.zh: “你到底在说 Beckie 的道德什么？Beckie 只是到处跟人上床？得了吧。”

cues.en: So don't label your particles by people's names,
cues.zh: 所以别用人名给粒子贴标签，

cues.en: is the short lesson here that we should learn.
cues.zh: 这就是我们该吸取的简短教训。

cues.en: But this is the big puzzle. This is it! This IS the puzzle that we are faced with,
cues.zh: 但这就是那个大谜题。就是这个！这就是我们面对的谜题，

cues.en: if you believe everything on the previous slides.
cues.zh: 如果你相信之前幻灯片上的一切。

cues.en: We have shown logically that the fact that the Hawking radiation comes from a region with "no drama",
cues.zh: 我们已经从逻辑上证明，霍金辐射来自一个“没有戏剧性”的区域，这一事实，

cues.en: flies through empty space, and eventually is going to bring all of its information back,
cues.zh: 飞过空旷空间，最终会把它的全部信息带回来，

cues.en: can't happen.
cues.zh: 不可能发生。

cues.en: Not all of those things can all happen at the same time,
cues.zh: 那些事情并非全都能同时发生，

cues.en: because entanglement is monogamous. Bob cannot be entangled with both Alice and Carrie
cues.zh: 因为纠缠具有单配性。Bob 不能同时与 Alice 和 Carrie 纠缠。

cues.en: Something has to go. This is the AMPS argument.
cues.zh: 总得舍弃点什么。这就是 AMPS 的论点。

cues.en: AMPS are Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski and Sully
cues.zh: AMPS 指的是 Almheiri、Marolf、Polchinski 和 Sully

cues.en: the Santa Barbarians who wrote this paper in 2012.
cues.zh: 2012 年写这篇论文的那些 Santa Barbarians。

cues.en: And they went through the list. They went through the list that Jennifer mentioned,
cues.zh: 然后他们逐条过了一遍清单。他们过了一遍 Jennifer 提到的那份清单，

cues.en: from Raphael Bousso, what could be going wrong?
cues.zh: 其中来自 Raphael Bousso 的那条：到底可能哪里出了问题？

cues.en: They are all kind of pretty dramatic.
cues.zh: 这些可能性都挺戏剧性的。

cues.en: One possibility is that information really is lost.
cues.zh: 一种可能是，信息真的会丢失。

cues.en: Maybe if you take encyclopaedia and throw them in the Black holes,
cues.zh: 也许你把百科全书扔进黑洞，

cues.en: the information in those books is truly lost forever, not just in practice, but even in principle.
cues.zh: 那些书里的信息就真的永远丢失了，不只是实际上，连原则上也是如此。

cues.en: That would be a dramatic violation of everything we think is true about quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 那将严重违背我们对量子力学的一切既有认知。

cues.en: In some sense that's OK. Everything that we think is true about quantum mechanics
cues.zh: 某种意义上这没问题。我们认为量子力学中所有为真的东西

cues.en: is a dramatic violation to what we thought about classical mechanics,
cues.zh: 都严重违背了我们过去对经典力学的认知，

cues.en: and yet it turns out to be right.
cues.zh: 但结果证明它是对的。

cues.en: It might be true that quantum mechanics is not the final theory of everything.
cues.zh: 量子力学可能并不是终极的万物理论。

cues.en: In fact , Stephen Hawking, who was the first to propose that this was true,
cues.zh: 事实上，Stephen Hawking 最早提出这可能是真的，

cues.en: said very explicitly that he thought this was the right answer.
cues.zh: 他非常明确地说过，他认为这就是正确答案。

cues.en: This is why he made that bet that he eventually conceded, and is now having second thoughts about conceding.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么他打了那个赌，最终认输，现在又对认输一事改变了想法。

cues.en: Despite the fact that it is a logical possibility that information is lost,
cues.zh: 尽管信息丢失在逻辑上是可能的，

cues.en: what we would really like to see is a well defined theory of how information is lost,
cues.zh: 我们真正希望看到的，是一个明确定义信息如何丢失的理论，

cues.en: where it goes, under what circumstances it is destroyed and conserved, and so forth.
cues.zh: 信息去了哪里，在什么情况下会被破坏、什么情况下守恒，等等。

cues.en: And nobody has been able to do that.
cues.zh: 但没人能做到这一点。

cues.en: So no one has been able to come up with a consistent coherent framework
cues.zh: 所以也没人能提出一个一致且自洽的框架，

cues.en: in which information really is lost.
cues.zh: 在其中信息确实会丢失。

cues.en: That's not to say it's not true.
cues.zh: 这并不是说它不成立。

cues.en: It's just that it's not one of those ideas that falls into your lap and everything suddenly makes sense.
cues.zh: 它不是那种自己送上门、然后一切突然都讲得通的想法。

cues.en: It's an idea that is suggested; you think about it, and it just becomes more and more puzzling as time goes on.
cues.zh: 这种想法只是被提出来；你越琢磨，随着时间推移反而越来越费解。

cues.en: Another possibility is locality. This is a somewhat subtle concept,
cues.zh: 另一种可能是定域性。这个概念有点微妙，

cues.en: but it's basically the idea that things that happen in the world happen in different locations in the world.
cues.zh: 但它基本是指，世界上发生的事都发生在世界上的不同地点。

cues.en: So a particle doesn't just pop out of existence here, and suddenly reappear over there.
cues.zh: 所以，粒子不会在这里凭空消失，又突然在那边出现。

cues.en: A particle propagates from here to there, obeying the laws of field theory,
cues.zh: 一个粒子从这里传播到那里，遵循场论的定律，

cues.en: of quantum field theory, in this case.
cues.zh: 在这个情形下，是量子场论的定律。

cues.en: This photon, or electron, or whatever it is that we labelled Bob,
cues.zh: 这个光子，或者电子，或者不管我们标记为 Bob 的是什么，

cues.en: moves from the event horizon to very very far away, following the laws of particle physics,
cues.zh: 从事件视界移动到非常非常远的地方，遵循粒子物理学的定律，

cues.en: which are local in space.
cues.zh: 这些定律在空间中是局域的。

cues.en: Maybe that's not what happens; maybe the information contained in Bob doesn't obey those laws.
cues.zh: 也许实际发生的并非如此；也许 Bob 中包含的信息并不遵守这些定律。

cues.en: That would be very dramatic and interesting.
cues.zh: 那会非常戏剧性，也非常有趣。

cues.en: Finally there is the possibility that, there is in fact "drama"at the event horizon.
cues.zh: 最后还有一种可能：事件视界处其实存在“戏剧性”。

cues.en: This thought that we've had since the 1960s, that Alice could fall into the event horizon and never notice anything,
cues.zh: 我们从1960年代起就有的这个想法——Alice 可以掉进事件视界，却完全不会察觉任何异常，

cues.en: is just not right.
cues.zh: 就是不对的。

cues.en: Instead, there is a tremendous amount of high energy radiation that Alice sees when she gets there.
cues.zh: 相反，当她到达那里时，会看到大量高能辐射。

cues.en: If you think about it, this Hawking radiation, it comes to you;
cues.zh: 仔细想想，这种霍金辐射是朝你而来的；

cues.en: it's very faint, it's very cold, it's very long-wavelength.
cues.zh: 它非常微弱，非常冷，波长也非常长。

cues.en: But when you leave a Black hole, a photon gets red-shifted; it loses energy.
cues.zh: 但当光子离开黑洞时，会发生红移；它会失去能量。

cues.en: It suffers what we call the gravitational red-shift.
cues.zh: 它会经历我们所说的引力红移。

cues.en: So a photon out here, that is very low energy,
cues.zh: 所以这里的一个光子，能量非常低，

cues.en: when we true it back in time, was very high energy, when it left.
cues.zh: 当我们把它在时间上回溯，它离开时其实能量非常高。

cues.en: Usually we say: Well, that's OK. It was high energy, but it was invisible because it was part of a quantum vacuum.
cues.zh: 通常我们会说：好吧，这没问题。它能量很高，但不可见，因为它是量子真空的一部分。

cues.en: And this idea is saying actually no. It was just there as a super-duper high energy particle.
cues.zh: 而这个观点其实是在说：不对。它当时就是以超级高能粒子的形式存在的。

cues.en: And when Alice tries to cross an event horizon, she would be incinerated by this wall of fire,
cues.zh: 当 Alice 试图穿过事件视界时，她会被这堵火墙烧成灰烬，

cues.en: all of these high energy particles lurking near the event horizon.
cues.zh: 所有这些潜伏在事件视界附近的高能粒子。

cues.en: And I fact, if this were true, there wouldn't even be anything called inside a Black Hole.
cues.zh: 而事实上，如果这是真的，黑洞内部甚至不会有任何所谓的东西。

cues.en: All the stuff that we think make up the Black hole would simply live on the event horizon.
cues.zh: 我们认为是构成黑洞的所有东西，都只会存在于事件视界上。

cues.en: Now be a very dramatic difference from how we think about Black holes were narrowing.
cues.zh: 这会和我们理解黑洞的方式形成极其鲜明的差异，而我们正在逐步缩小范围。

cues.en: Sadly, neither Almheiri, Marold, Polchinski or Sully seemed to know that
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，Almheiri、Marold、Polchinski 和 Sully 似乎都不知道

cues.en: the word Firewall is used in computer science,
cues.zh: Firewall 这个词在计算机科学中，

cues.en: to be a good thing, to stop evil people from getting in where you wanna go.
cues.zh: 是件好事，能阻止坏人进入你想去的地方。

cues.en: They used it as a bad thing, something that burns you to bits, as you fall into a black hole.
cues.zh: 他们却把它当成坏事，一种当你掉进黑洞时把你烧成灰的东西。

cues.en: So the smart money, among people who are my personal friends,
cues.zh: 所以，在我的私人朋友里，懂行的人押注的是，

cues.en: is that locality is going to be the thing to go.
cues.zh: 局域性将会成为被放弃的那一个。

cues.en: It is a very dramatic thing, but it seems to be a little bit easier to live with than the other two, going.
cues.zh: 这非常戏剧化，但比起另外两个也被放弃，似乎还稍微容易接受一点。

cues.en: So let me talk a little more about locality.
cues.zh: 让我再稍微讲讲局部性。

cues.en: As Jennifer mentioned, you can visualise what locality is by thinking about
cues.zh: 正如 Jennifer 提到的，你可以通过想象下面这个情景来理解局部性是什么：

cues.en: what happens when you drop a pebble into a pond,
cues.zh: 把一颗小石子丢进池塘时会发生什么，

cues.en: or when you make a sound, or when you flash a light , or anything like that.
cues.zh: 或者你发出声音、闪一下光，或做类似事情时会发生什么。

cues.en: The effects of what you do
cues.zh: 你所做事情产生的影响

cues.en: do not show up all throughout the universe instantaneously.
cues.zh: 不会瞬间出现在整个宇宙中。

cues.en: They move at a certain rate - the speed of light,
cues.zh: 它们以一定的速度传播——光速、

cues.en: the speed of sound, or the speed of waves in the water
cues.zh: 声速，或水波的速度。

cues.en: They move from one place to the next to next to the next.
cues.zh: 它们从一个地方传到下一个、再下一个、再下一个地方。

cues.en: That's a reflection of the fact that the way we talk about the world
cues.zh: 这反映了一个事实：我们谈论世界的方式，

cues.en: is by talking about what's happening at every point in space.
cues.zh: 就是谈论空间中每一点正在发生什么。

cues.en: So this is space, if I were to tell you what's happening in some region of space,
cues.zh: 这里是空间，如果我要告诉你空间某个区域内发生了什么，

cues.en: I tell you what's happening there, or what's happening there, and so forth.
cues.zh: 我就告诉你那里发生了什么，或者那里发生了什么，等等。

cues.en: If someone says: What's going on in this lecture hall?
cues.zh: 如果有人说：这个报告厅里正在发生什么？

cues.en: I can tell them - the identity of every person and every seat in the lecture hall, and what they are doing.
cues.zh: 我可以告诉他——报告厅里每个人、每个座位是谁，以及他们在做什么。

cues.en: Separate information in every point in space.
cues.zh: 把信息分散到空间中的每一个点上。

cues.en: Now quantum mechanics complicates this a little bit,
cues.zh: 不过量子力学让这件事稍微复杂了一点，

cues.en: because it says that there could be separate superpositions in classical realities.
cues.zh: 因为它说，经典现实中可以存在彼此分离的叠加态。

cues.en: But each on elf those classical realities is local in space.
cues.zh: 但这些经典现实中的每一个，在空间上都是局域的。

cues.en: There is a description of ... there are so many electrons over here, so many photons over there,
cues.zh: 有一种描述是……这边有这么多电子，那边有那么多光子，

cues.en: Everything is defined by where it is in space.
cues.zh: 一切都是由它在空间中的位置来定义的。

cues.en: That is the principle of locality.
cues.zh: 这就是局域性原理。

cues.en: Entanglement makes the concept of locality a little bit more problematic,
cues.zh: 纠缠让局域性这个概念变得有点麻烦，

cues.en: but it doesn't break it; it just makes it more interesting.
cues.zh: 但它并没有破坏局域性，只是让它变得更有趣。

cues.en: The quantum state of these two particles that are very very far away from each other is not local.
cues.zh: 这两个相距极其遥远的粒子的量子态并不是局域的。

cues.en: However, the dynamics, how they actually change with time, how you can actually send a signal through space,
cues.zh: 然而，动力学，也就是它们随时间实际如何变化、你如何能在空间中实际传递信号，

cues.en: is all perfectly local, even with quantum mechanics and entanglement.
cues.zh: 则完全是局域的，即便在量子力学和纠缠存在的情况下也是如此。

cues.en: If you want something to happen, you just start it here
cues.zh: 如果你想让某件事发生，只要在这里启动它

cues.en: and you just travel through space to get anywhere else.
cues.zh: 然后只要在空间中穿行，就能到达任何地方。

cues.en: Despite the fact that locality is very precious to us,
cues.zh: 尽管局域性对我们来说非常宝贵，

cues.en: it's probably not right.
cues.zh: 它可能并不正确。

cues.en: In fact, other thought experiments involving Black holes have already given us reasons to believe that,
cues.zh: 事实上，其他涉及黑洞的思想实验已经让我们有理由相信，

cues.en: when it comes to quantum gravity, just what we are doing here, after all,
cues.zh: 在量子引力方面，我们在这里所做的，毕竟正是

cues.en: quantising gravity itself, the fabric of space-time.
cues.zh: 把引力本身——时空的结构——量子化。

cues.en: When it comes to quantum gravity, locality is probably not an inviolable principle.
cues.zh: 说到量子引力，局域性很可能不是一条不可侵犯的原则。

cues.en: The question is, how much violation with locality can we get away with?
cues.zh: 问题是，我们能在多大程度上违反局域性而不出问题？

cues.en: To what extent is the universe not really described by what's happening here,
cues.zh: 宇宙究竟在多大程度上并非由这里发生的事来描述，

cues.en: plus what's happening there, plus what's happening there?
cues.zh: 再加上那里发生的事，再加上那里发生的事？

cues.en: So we have two clues that are given to us, by thinking about Black holes.
cues.zh: 所以，思考黑洞给了我们两条线索。

cues.en: One is called the holographic principle.
cues.zh: 其中一条叫全息原理。

cues.en: This actually goes back to Stephen Hawking once again, and his radiation from Black holes.
cues.zh: 这其实又要回到 Stephen Hawking，以及他提出的黑洞辐射。

cues.en: One of the implications of Hawking's discovery that Black holes radiate,
cues.zh: Hawking 发现黑洞会辐射，其中一个推论是，

cues.en: by the way, I should (because I'm in a venerable lecture hall), stop saying,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我应该——毕竟我在一座久负盛名的讲堂里——别再说，

cues.en: we have never seen a radiating Black hole.
cues.zh: 我们从未见过正在辐射的黑洞。

cues.en: This is not data that we are talking about here.
cues.zh: 我们这里谈的并不是数据。

cues.en: I'm sure that Black holes radiate; my confidence is very very high,
cues.zh: 我确信黑洞会辐射；我的把握非常高，

cues.en: but I could be wrong about that.
cues.zh: 但我也可能在这件事上错了。

cues.en: It's cherished rules of physics that tell us that black holes radiate,
cues.zh: 物理学中那些珍贵的定律告诉我们，黑洞会辐射，

cues.en: but it sure would be nice to have some experiments or some data that said the same thing.
cues.zh: 但要是能有实验或数据印证这一点，那当然就更好了。

cues.en: Alright. Thought to the experimental is now complete,
cues.zh: 好了，从理论到实验这一步现在完成了，

cues.en: now we can go back to crazy theorists' land.
cues.zh: 现在我们可以回到疯狂理论家的世界了。

cues.en: Hawking showed that a Black hole actually has a lot of entropy.
cues.zh: 霍金指出，黑洞其实拥有很大的熵。

cues.en: Entropy is a way of talking about the disorderliness, the chaoticness of an arrangement of stuff in the universe.
cues.zh: 熵是用来描述宇宙中物质排列有多无序、多混乱的一种方式。

cues.en: When cream and coffee are all mixed together, they are high entropy;
cues.zh: 当奶油和咖啡完全混合在一起时，它们处于高熵状态；

cues.en: when they are separated, they are low entropy.
cues.zh: 当它们彼此分开时，则处于低熵状态。

cues.en: So ordinarily, if you want to quantify actually the amount of entropy in the air in this room,
cues.zh: 所以通常来说，如果你想真正量化这个房间空气里有多少熵，

cues.en: you just talk about the numbers of ways you can rearrange the molecules that make up the air in this room.
cues.zh: 你只需要考虑：把构成这间屋子空气的分子重新排列，有多少种方式。

cues.en: And the number of ways that you can rearrange the molecules just depends on the volume of space that we have in the room.
cues.zh: 而分子重新排列的方式数量，只取决于这间屋子所拥有的空间体积。

cues.en: So it is an absolute rock-solid feature of entropy in the ordinary experimental macroscopic world,
cues.zh: 所以，在普通的实验宏观世界中，熵有一个绝对可靠的特征，

cues.en: that entropy scales like the volume of the system that you are looking at.
cues.zh: 那就是熵会随你所观察系统的体积按比例缩放。

cues.en: If you double the volume, you will double the available entropy.
cues.zh: 如果你把体积翻倍，可用熵也会翻倍。

cues.en: What Hawking showed is that for a Black hole,
cues.zh: Hawking 所证明的是，对于黑洞而言，

cues.en: the entropy of a black hole scales as the area of its event horizon.
cues.zh: 黑洞的熵与其事件视界的面积成正比。

cues.en: So a Black hole has a volume; there is a volume inside the event horizon.
cues.zh: 所以黑洞有体积；事件视界内部存在一个体积。

cues.en: There is a three-dimensional volume enclosed by the event horizon.
cues.zh: 有一个被事件视界包围的三维体积。

cues.en: You might have guessed, that the entropy of a Black hole is proportional to that volume inside.
cues.zh: 你可能已经猜到，黑洞的熵正比于内部的那个体积。

cues.en: That is not right.
cues.zh: 这是不对的。

cues.en: It is proportional to the area, some two-dimensional quantity,
cues.zh: 它正比于面积，某个二维量，

cues.en: the area of the event horizon, not the three-dimensional quantity of the volume inside.
cues.zh: 事件视界的面积，而不是内部体积的三维量。

cues.en: People had known that for a long time;
cues.zh: 人们早就知道这一点；

cues.en: It didn't really sink in seriously until the 1990s,
cues.zh: 但直到1990年代，它才真正被认真领会，

cues.en: when , Huskin and others promoted this idea,
cues.zh: 当时 Huskin 等人推动了这一想法，

cues.en: to not just a weird idosyncrasy of Black holes,
cues.zh: 使其不再只是黑洞的某种古怪特性，

cues.en: but a fundamental feature of nature.
cues.zh: 而是自然界的一个基本特征。

cues.en: They proposed the holographic principle,
cues.zh: 他们提出了全息原理，

cues.en: that says that basically any time, you think you had a three-dimension collection of stuff,
cues.zh: 它基本上是说，任何时候你以为自己面对的是一堆三维的东西，

cues.en: like us here in this room.
cues.zh: 就像我们在这个房间里一样。

cues.en: All of the information needed to describe us can be compressed into one two-dimensional surface.
cues.zh: 描述我们所需要的一切信息，都能压缩进一个二维表面。

cues.en: In a black hole, it becomes frighteningly real.
cues.zh: 而在黑洞里，这一点变得真实得令人不安。

cues.en: In a black hole, the two-dimensional event horizon really does contain all the information you need,
cues.zh: 在黑洞中，二维的事件视界确实包含了所需的全部信息，

cues.en: to talk about what's happening inside, according to the holographic principle.
cues.zh: 根据全息原理，这些信息足以描述内部正在发生的一切。

cues.en: But it should be true even in this room, or the galaxy or the universe.
cues.zh: 但这在这个房间里也应该成立，在星系或整个宇宙中也一样。

cues.en: And if that is true, locality is being dramatically violated,
cues.zh: 而如果这一点成立，那定域性就被严重破坏了，

cues.en: because there is a lot less that can possibly happen in this room than you thought could.
cues.zh: 因为这个房间里可能发生的事情，比你想象的少得多。

cues.en: You thought that something could be happening here, and something could be happening there,
cues.zh: 你以为这里可能有事在发生，那里也可能有事在发生，

cues.en: and different things could be happening at every point.
cues.zh: 每个点上都可以有不同的事情在发生。

cues.en: But the holographic principle says: No, that's not true.
cues.zh: 但全息原理说：不，事实并非如此。

cues.en: One of the arguments for it, is if you imagine all of the different possible things that could happen
cues.zh: 支持这一观点的论据之一是，如果你想象所有可能发生的不同事情

cues.en: most of them would have a lot of energy and would collapse to make a Black hole.
cues.zh: 其中大多数都会携带大量能量，并坍缩形成黑洞。

cues.en: So there is an upper limit on the number of things that could happen in this room,
cues.zh: 所以这个房间里可能发生的事情数量存在一个上限，

cues.en: and the size of the upper limit is proportional to the area of the walls around this room.
cues.zh: 而这个上限的大小，与这个房间四周墙壁的面积成正比。

cues.en: So there is this hypothesis that all of physics really lives in a world
cues.zh: 于是就有了这样一个假说：整个物理学其实生活在一个

cues.en: that is one dimension lower than the world we actually see.
cues.zh: 比我们实际所见世界低一个维度的世界里。

cues.en: And again, we are trying to make sense of this idea. We are making progress, but we are not completely there yet.
cues.zh: 我们还是想弄明白这个想法。我们有进展，但还没完全搞定。

cues.en: The other idea that has come out of Black holes and argues against locality is called Black hole complementarity.
cues.zh: 黑洞研究里还提出了另一个反对局域性的想法，叫黑洞互补性。

cues.en: Remember I said that, from the point of view of Bob from far away,
cues.zh: 记得我说过，从远处 Bob 的角度看，

cues.en: he sees radiation coming out of the Black hole, and he says: well if I trace it backwards,
cues.zh: 他看到黑洞发出辐射，然后说：好吧，如果我把这辐射往回追溯，

cues.en: it must have been very high energy radiation when it left the event horizon.
cues.zh: 那它离开事件视界时一定是极高能的辐射。

cues.en: Whereas Alice, in the conventional way of thinking about things,
cues.zh: 而在传统思维方式中，Alice

cues.en: passes through the event horizon and sees nothing there
cues.zh: 穿过事件视界后，在那里什么也看不到

cues.en: just empty space.
cues.zh: 只有空无一物的空间。

cues.en: So they had incompatible ways of describing the same situation.
cues.zh: 所以他们对同一情境的描述方式互不兼容。

cues.en: Bob thinks the event horizon is bubbling with high-energy radiation;
cues.zh: Bob 认为事件视界上翻涌着高能辐射；

cues.en: Alice says there's nothing there.
cues.zh: Alice 却说那里什么都没有。

cues.en: Black hole complementarity says: they are both correct.
cues.zh: 黑洞互补性原理说：他们俩都对。

cues.en: Black hole complementarity says they are different-sounding ways
cues.zh: 黑洞互补性原理说，它们是听起来不同的方式，

cues.en: of giving equivalent descriptions of the same fundamental underlying reality,
cues.zh: 用来对同一个底层基本现实给出等价描述，

cues.en: and that two things that are seen by two observers can look very very different,
cues.zh: 而且两个观察者所看到的东西可能看起来非常非常不同，

cues.en: as long as the observers can never get together to compare notes.
cues.zh: 只要这些观察者永远无法碰面核对笔记。

cues.en: So what happens is, if you give Bob enough time to collect the Hawking radiation,
cues.zh: 所以情况是这样：如果你给 Bob 足够的时间去收集霍金辐射，

cues.en: and figure out what he thinks the horizon looks like,
cues.zh: 并弄清他认为视界是什么样子，

cues.en: and you give Alice enough time to fall into the horizon.
cues.zh: 再给 Alice 足够的时间落入视界。
