cues.en: If Bob then says: alright, I've got some data; I know what's coming out of the Black hole.
cues.zh: 如果 Bob 然后说：好吧，我拿到了一些数据；我知道从黑洞里出来的是什么。

cues.en: I am going to fly into the Black hole and tell Alice what I saw.
cues.zh: 我要飞进黑洞，告诉 Alice 我看到了什么。

cues.en: It is too late. She has been spaghettified and crushed into the singularity.
cues.zh: 但已经太晚了。她已经被拉成面条，并被压进奇点。

cues.en: So these two observers see a very different thing happening in the world, but hey can never talk about it.
cues.zh: 所以这两个观察者看到世上发生的事截然不同，但他们永远没法就此交流。

cues.en: Only we - God-like physicists, looking at the whole thing from afar,
cues.zh: 只有我们——像上帝一样的物理学家，从远处俯瞰整个局面，

cues.en: can give the bird's eye view on everything that is going on.
cues.zh: 才能对正在发生的一切给出鸟瞰式的全景。

cues.en: That is the principle of Black hole complementarity.
cues.zh: 这就是黑洞互补性原理。

cues.en: It's borrowed from the early days of quantum mechanics when Niels Bohr pointed out that
cues.zh: 它借自量子力学的早期，当时尼尔斯·玻尔指出，

cues.en: you are allowed to measure position, OR you are allowed to measure velocity.
cues.zh: 你要么可以测量位置，要么可以测量速度。

cues.en: You are not allowed to measure both at the same time.
cues.zh: 你不能同时测量两者。

cues.en: That was quantum complementarity; this is Black hole complementarity.
cues.zh: 那是量子互补性；这是黑洞互补性。

cues.en: So again, it's a violation of locality in some sense.
cues.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，这又违反了局域性。

cues.en: It says that the right way to describe the world isn't what's happening here, and what's happening there,
cues.zh: 它说的是，描述世界的正确方式，并不是这里发生什么、那里发生什么，

cues.en: and what's happening there, and what's happening there, separately.
cues.zh: 以及那里发生什么、那里发生什么，分开来看。

cues.en: What's happening right there can depend in a very dramatic way
cues.zh: 那里正在发生什么，可能以极其显著的方式取决于

cues.en: on who's looking at it and from what perspective.
cues.zh: 谁在看它、从什么视角看。

cues.en: So somehow, all the information about what's going on in the world
cues.zh: 所以不知怎么地，关于世界中正在发生的一切信息

cues.en: is not simply located in individual points in space.
cues.zh: 并不只是存在于空间中的各个点上。

cues.en: It's encoded in some cryptic way that we don't yet understand,
cues.zh: 它以一种我们尚未理解的隐秘方式被编码，

cues.en: and that's what we are trying to get at, by doing these thought experiments.
cues.zh: 而这正是我们通过做这些思想实验想要弄清楚的。

cues.en: The problem is, these two types of non-locality,
cues.zh: 问题是，这两种非定域性，

cues.en: don't seem to be enough to solve the Firewall puzzle.
cues.zh: 似乎不足以解决防火墙谜题。

cues.en: Remember in the holographic principle, you say: OK, all the information is there on the horizon.
cues.zh: 还记得在全息原理里，你会说：好，所有信息都在视界上。

cues.en: That doesn't tell you anything at all about what you see, when you fall into the horizon.
cues.zh: 这根本没有告诉你，当你落入视界时会看到什么。

cues.en: And in the complementarity, you explicitly say that Alice, when she falls in, doesn't see anything at the horizon
cues.zh: 而在互补性中，你明确说 Alice 掉进去时，在视界处什么也看不到

cues.en: but it's just an assertion.
cues.zh: 但这只是一个断言。

cues.en: You are not explaining how the entanglements can actually work.
cues.zh: 你并没有解释这些纠缠实际上如何运作。

cues.en: The force of the Black hole Firewall paradox,
cues.zh: 黑洞火墙悖论的威力，

cues.en: as in the amount of non-locality you seem to need to make physics work,
cues.zh: 也就是为了让物理成立而似乎需要的非定域性程度，

cues.en: is even worse than that given to us by the holographic principle or complementarity.
cues.zh: 甚至比全息原理或互补性给我们的还要糟糕。

cues.en: So what could be going on, and again, nobody knows what's going on,
cues.zh: 那么可能发生了什么，而且再说一次，没人知道发生了什么，

cues.en: so we'll tell you two crazy-sounding ideas.
cues.zh: 所以我们要告诉你两个听起来很疯狂的想法。

cues.en: The hope is that they are just crazy enough to be right.
cues.zh: 希望它们疯狂得刚刚好，以至于可能是对的。

cues.en: One idea is that, there really isn't any such thing as "inside the Black hole".
cues.zh: 其中一个想法是，其实根本不存在所谓“黑洞内部”这回事。

cues.en: This idea is that, what you think of as "inside the Black hole",
cues.zh: 这个想法是说，你所认为的“黑洞内部”，

cues.en: is just a copy of certain things going on outside the Black hole.
cues.zh: 只不过是黑洞外部发生的某些事情的一个副本。

cues.en: This is a little bit strange to get it straight, because in fact, in quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 这有点难以理清，因为事实上，在量子力学中，

cues.en: there is a rule that says: you can't copy things.
cues.zh: 有一条规则说：你不能复制东西。

cues.en: There is what's playfully called the no-Xerox theorem, or the no-cloning theorem.
cues.zh: 有个被戏称为“不可复印定理”的东西，也叫不可克隆定理。

cues.en: You have the quantum bit of information. You can move it，
cues.zh: 你有一个量子比特的信息。你可以移动它，

cues.en: and you can evolve it and so forth, but you can't just copy it without destroying it.
cues.zh: 也可以让它演化等等，但不能不摧毁它就把它复制出来。

cues.en: But this is saying something more profound than that.
cues.zh: 但这说的比那更深刻。

cues.en: It's not that you fall in and there is a copy of you that goes in and a copy of you that goes out.
cues.zh: 并不是说你掉进去后，有一个你的副本进去、一个你的副本出来。

cues.en: It is saying that the interior of a Black hole really is exactly the same thing,
cues.zh: 它说的是，黑洞内部其实完全就是同一个东西，

cues.en: as the exterior secretly,
cues.zh: 秘密地等同于外部，

cues.en: secretly encoded in some weird way.
cues.zh: 以某种古怪的方式被秘密编码。

cues.en: So the difference is that if I can take a quantum mechanical object,
cues.zh: 所以区别在于，如果我能拿一个量子力学对象，

cues.en: and clone it, then I could separately do things to this one and then do separate things to this one.
cues.zh: 并把它克隆，那我就能对这个做点事，再对那个做点别的事。

cues.en: But this is saying that literally everything that happens inside the event horizon,
cues.zh: 但这里说的是，事件视界内部字面意义上发生的一切，

cues.en: is mirrored in some exactly equivalent way by things going on outside the event horizon.
cues.zh: 都会以某种完全等价的方式，由事件视界之外发生的事情镜像出来。

cues.en: That is a set of words that we can say.
cues.zh: 这是一组我们能说出来的词。

cues.en: Those are all English sentences that are more or less grammatical.
cues.zh: 这些都是英语句子，而且或多或少合乎语法。

cues.en: We don't really have a quantitated theory about how this would work.
cues.zh: 我们其实还没有关于这如何运作的定量理论。

cues.en: It would in fact solve the Black hole Firewall puzzle,
cues.zh: 事实上，它能解决黑洞防火墙之谜，

cues.en: because this thing that we thought was a photon falling in, labelled Alice,
cues.zh: 因为我们原以为掉进去的是一个光子，标记为 Alice，

cues.en: was exactly Bob all along, or one of the other photons.
cues.zh: 其实它一直都是 Bob，或者是另一个光子。

cues.en: It seems dramatic but it might actually be true.
cues.zh: 这听起来很戏剧化，但也许确实是真的。

cues.en: And then just to go one step weirder, we have what is playfully called ER=EPR.
cues.zh: 再往更奇怪的方向走一步，就是我们戏称为 ER=EPR 的东西。

cues.en: This is an idea of again Leonard Susskind and Juan Maldacena.
cues.zh: 这同样是 Leonard Susskind 和 Juan Maldacena 的想法。

cues.en: EPR, we already mentioned - Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen, are the ones who first took quantum entanglement
cues.zh: EPR，我们已经提过——Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen——是最早把量子纠缠

cues.en: put it front-and-centre.
cues.zh: 推到核心位置的人。

cues.en: ER was just Einstein ad Rosen; Podolsky didn't get involved, but it was a paper written I think the same year
cues.zh: ER 只是 Einstein 和 Rosen；Podolsky 没有参与，但那篇论文我想是同一年写的

cues.en: as the EPR paper, but on a totally different subject,
cues.zh: 和 EPR 论文同一年，但主题完全不同，

cues.en: about the idea that, given general relativity, given the idea that space can be curved and dynamical,
cues.zh: 讲的是这样一个想法：给定广义相对论，给定空间可以弯曲且具有动力学性质，

cues.en: you could imagine building little bridges in space-time that we call wormholes.
cues.zh: 你可以想象在时空中建造一些我们称之为虫洞的小桥。

cues.en: So Einstein and Rosen, what we call an Einstein-Rosen bridge,
cues.zh: So Einstein 和 Rosen，也就是我们所说的 Einstein-Rosen 桥，

cues.en: is just a connection between two widely separated pieces of universe,
cues.zh: 它只是宇宙中两块相距遥远的部分之间的连接，

cues.en: maybe that look like Black holes from the outside.
cues.zh: 从外面看，它们可能像黑洞。

cues.en: The trick here is that, you think the distance between this Black hole and this Black hole is very large,
cues.zh: 这里的妙处在于，你以为这个黑洞和那个黑洞之间的距离非常远，

cues.en: if you travel this way, but secretly it can be very short if you take the shortcut through the wormhole.
cues.zh: 如果你沿着这条路走确实如此，但如果你走虫洞这条捷径，距离可能偷偷地非常短。

cues.en: This was the Einstein-Rosen suggestion.
cues.zh: 这就是 Einstein-Rosen 的提议。

cues.en: It was a little bit speculative,
cues.zh: 这有点推测性，

cues.en: but it went into the toolbox of theoretical physicists.
cues.zh: 但它进入了理论物理学家的工具箱。

cues.en: And it had nothing to do with entanglement or quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 它与量子纠缠或量子力学毫无关系，

cues.en: and Maldacena and Susskind was saying is that, well actually maybe it does.
cues.zh: 而 Maldacena 和 Susskind 说，其实也许有关系。

cues.en: Maybe when two particles are quantum entangled,
cues.zh: 也许当两个粒子处于量子纠缠时，

cues.en: secretly, there is effectively a little tiny wormhole that is connecting them,
cues.zh: 暗中其实存在一个微小的虫洞把它们连接起来，

cues.en: that for certain purposes,
cues.zh: 出于某些目的，

cues.en: you can think of quantum entanglement as being enforced by a little bridge in space-time,
cues.zh: 你可以把量子纠缠看作由时空中一座小桥所维持，

cues.en: that brings those two particles together.
cues.zh: 这座小桥把这两个粒子连接在一起。

cues.en: So the way that information can get out of a Black hole, in this idea,
cues.zh: 所以在这个设想里，信息逃出黑洞的方式，

cues.en: is that Black hole is connected with by little virtual wormholes
cues.zh: 就是黑洞通过微小的虚拟虫洞，

cues.en: to all the particles that are being emitted as Hawking radiation.
cues.zh: 与所有以霍金辐射形式发射出的粒子相连。

cues.en: Really, the importance of this suggestion is that space-time is not fundamental.
cues.zh: 其实，这个设想的重要性在于：时空并不是基本的。

cues.en: Space-time is an approximation
cues.zh: 时空只是一种近似，

cues.en: that comes out of thinking about quantum states and how they are entangled with each other.
cues.zh: 它来自对量子态以及它们如何相互纠缠的思考。

cues.en: we live in space-time; we tend to think that space and time are kind of important.
cues.zh: 我们生活在时空中；我们往往认为空间和时间挺重要的。

cues.en: This point of view is saying: they are just good ideas.
cues.zh: 这种观点是说：它们只是些好用的概念。

cues.en: They are nothing absolutely fundamental; they are just a good approximation.
cues.zh: 它们根本不是绝对基础的东西，只是一个好的近似。

cues.en: And finally of course, there is the other possibility that Firewalls are real.
cues.zh: 最后当然还有另一种可能：Firewall 是真实存在的。

cues.en: That we've been wrong for the past 50 years
cues.zh: 也就是过去 50 年我们都错了

cues.en: when we are thinking about what would happen when you fall into a Black hole.
cues.zh: 在思考掉进黑洞会发生什么的时候。

cues.en: It would not be painless until you got spaghettified.
cues.zh: 在被意大利面化之前，这都不会是无痛的。

cues.en: It would be painful long before then.
cues.zh: 远在那之前，就已经很痛苦了。

cues.en: This is the old picture of Black holes. You would just fall in and nothing would happen.
cues.zh: 这是黑洞的旧图景。你只会掉进去，什么也不会发生。

cues.en: And maybe that's completely wrong. Maybe in fact, there is a wall of ultra-high energy radiation
cues.zh: 也许这完全错了。也许事实上存在一堵超高能辐射墙

cues.en: that incinerates you to bits long before you fall into the event horizon,
cues.zh: 在你落入事件视界之前很久，就把你烧成碎片，

cues.en: and would be spaghettified.
cues.zh: 而不是等到你被意大利面化。

cues.en: Again, that seems weird to us,
cues.zh: 再说，这在我们看来很奇怪，

cues.en: because the horizon in classical general relativity, not only is nothing going on there,
cues.zh: 因为在经典广义相对论中，视界那里不仅什么都没发生，

cues.en: but the gravitational field isn't even that strong.
cues.zh: 而且引力场甚至都没那么强。

cues.en: We think of, if you are right next to a Black hole, the gravitational field better be pretty strong.
cues.zh: 我们会想，如果你就紧挨着黑洞，引力场总该非常强吧。

cues.en: But it's really just, it's so big that you don't notice.
cues.zh: 但其实只是，它太大了，你根本察觉不到。

cues.en: You would not be spaghettified at the event horizon.
cues.zh: 在事件视界处，你不会被拉成面条。

cues.en: You are not spaghettified until you are well inside, an astrophysically large Black hole.
cues.zh: 只有深入到天体物理尺度的大黑洞内部，你才会被拉成面条。

cues.en: So this idea is saying that, in a region of space-time, that should seem perfectly benign and happy,
cues.zh: 所以这个想法是说，在一个看似完全温和无害的时空区域里，

cues.en: something really dramatic is going on.
cues.zh: 却有非常剧烈的事情在发生。

cues.en: That may be true; if so that would be a very important discovery.
cues.zh: 这也许是真的；若果真如此，那将是一项非常重要的发现。

cues.en: So to conclude: why is this important? Why does this matter?
cues.zh: 那么总结一下：为什么这很重要？为什么这件事有关系？

cues.en: And we could have started by telling you why it matters, but you are already here,
cues.zh: 我们本可以先告诉你它为什么重要，但既然你已经在这儿了，

cues.en: so we figured that you'd go along.
cues.zh: 所以我们觉得你会继续听下去。

cues.en: The point is that trying to quantise gravity
cues.zh: 关键在于，试图量子化引力

cues.en: is probably the most important outstanding puzzle in fundamental theoretical physics,
cues.zh: 很可能是基础理论物理中最重要的未解难题，

cues.en: the ultimate description that we have of how nature works at a deep level.
cues.zh: 也是我们对自然在深层如何运作所拥有的终极描述。

cues.en: We have a very very good theory of particle physics, quantum mechanics, and space-time.
cues.zh: 我们有一个非常非常好的理论，涵盖粒子物理、量子力学和时空。

cues.en: The quantum mechanics part doesn't play well together with the space-time part
cues.zh: 量子力学那部分和时空那部分配合得不太好

cues.en: and that's the search for quantum gravity.
cues.zh: 这就是对量子引力的探索。

cues.en: But to get a theory of quantum gravity, we need to know what it is that we are quantising.
cues.zh: 但要得到量子引力理论，我们得知道我们要量子化的到底是什么。

cues.en: We think that we understand classical gravity; Einstein told us what it is. it's the curvature of space-time,
cues.zh: 我们认为自己理解经典引力；爱因斯坦告诉我们它是什么：它是时空的曲率，

cues.en: but all of these ideas from Black holes, getting the information out, the holographic principle, complementarity, Firewalls;
cues.zh: 但从黑洞、把信息取出来，到全息原理、互补性、防火墙，

cues.en: all of them are telling us that space-time itself is not fundamental,
cues.zh: 所有这些想法都在告诉我们：时空本身不是基本的，

cues.en: that when we talk about space-time, it's like talking about the air in this room as some kind of fluid,
cues.zh: 当我们谈论时空时，就像把这房间里的空气说成某种流体，

cues.en: that has a temperature, a pressure, and a velocity, and a speed of sound and so forth.
cues.zh: 它有温度、压力、速度、声速等等。

cues.en: But we know, and you and I know that if you look closely enough at the air in this room, it is no longer fluid,
cues.zh: 但我们知道，你我都知道，如果你足够仔细地观察这个房间里的空气，它就不再是流体，

cues.en: it resolves into different atoms and molecules.
cues.zh: 它会分解成各种原子和分子。

cues.en: This kind of idea is saying, sure, space-time is a nice approximate way to talk about the world,
cues.zh: 这种想法是说，当然，时空是一种谈论世界的不错近似方式，

cues.en: but when you really push it, it breaks down and needs to be replaced by something else.
cues.zh: 但当你真正深究时，它会失效，需要被别的东西取代。

cues.en: We have no idea what that something-else is. That's the problem.
cues.zh: 我们根本不知道那个别的东西是什么。问题就在这儿。

cues.en: If quantum gravity is not a theory of space-time curvature being quantised,
cues.zh: 如果量子引力并不是关于时空曲率被量子化的理论，

cues.en: it is a theory of something else being quantised,
cues.zh: 那它就是关于别的东西被量子化的理论，

cues.en: something that is related to the space-time we observe every day in some mysterious, non-local way,
cues.zh: 这个“别的东西”以某种神秘的非局域方式，与我们每天观测到的时空相关联，

cues.en: that we haven't fully understood.
cues.zh: 而我们还没完全理解它。

cues.en: We are some provocative clues; we have some toy models, that seem to give us useful information,
cues.zh: 我们有一些颇具启发的线索；也有一些玩具模型，似乎能提供有用的信息，

cues.en: but we are nowhere near the final answer yet.
cues.zh: 但离最终答案还差得远。

cues.en: That is what makes it fun; that is why this is a fun thing to think about.
cues.zh: 这正是它有趣的地方；也正是为什么思考它很有意思。

cues.en: It is not going to cure cancer or build a better iPhone,
cues.zh: 它不会治愈癌症，也不会造出更好的 iPhone，

cues.en: thinking about the holographic principle and Black hole Firewalls.
cues.zh: 思考全息原理和黑洞火墙。

cues.en: All that it will help us do, is understand at a deeper level what the fundamental nature of reality is.
cues.zh: 它能帮我们做的全部，就是更深入地理解现实的根本本质是什么。

cues.en: And I think that is something that is well worth thinking about.
cues.zh: 而我认为，这非常值得思考。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: [APPLAUSE]
cues.zh: [掌声]

cues.en: So now we have plenty of time for questions. I am going to bring up my lovely wife again.
cues.zh: 现在我们有充足的时间提问。我要再次请我可爱的妻子上台。

cues.en: We were told - I don't know if this is true -
cues.zh: 我们被告知——不知道这是不是真的——

cues.en: we were told that the last time as husband-and-wife team spoke at the Royal Institution,
cues.zh: 我们被告知，上一次有夫妻搭档在皇家研究院演讲，

cues.en: it was Marie and Pierre Curie.
cues.zh: 是 Marie and Pierre Curie。

cues.en: And they didn't let her talk.
cues.zh: 他们没让她说话。

cues.en: Come a long way. Alright, way up, right in the middle.
cues.zh: 走了很远。好，往上，正中间。

cues.en: MAN: Thanks. I have a question about the human Alice and Bob, which is probably just misunderstanding.
cues.zh: 男：谢谢。我有个关于人类 Alice 和 Bob 的问题，可能只是我理解错了。

cues.en: When Bob is watching Alice enter the Black hole,
cues.zh: 当 Bob 看着 Alice 进入黑洞时，

cues.en: she basically freezes in space, and he doesn't actually see her
cues.zh: 她基本上冻结在太空中，而他实际上看不到她

cues.en: well, and infinite amount of time would possibly pass before she enters the Black hole.
cues.zh: 嗯，而且在她进入黑洞之前，可能已经过去了无限长的时间。

cues.en: When I was young, there were still ideas about the Big Crunch,
cues.zh: 我年轻时，人们还有关于大挤压的想法，

cues.en: and I was thinking Alice can never get to the singularity,
cues.zh: 我当时想，Alice 永远到不了奇点，

cues.en: because time is basically slowed down so much from the point of view of Bob and the rest of the universe
cues.zh: 因为从 Bob 和宇宙其他部分的视角看，时间被减慢得太厉害了

cues.en: that the Big Crunch will happen before she ever gets there.
cues.zh: 以至于在她到达那里之前，大挤压就会发生。

cues.en: Now obviously the Big Crunch might not happen because of dark energy,
cues.zh: 显然，由于暗能量，大挤压可能不会发生，

cues.en: but as the black hole evaporates,
cues.zh: 但随着黑洞蒸发，

cues.en: would the evaporation of the Black hole not sort of overtake Alice reaching the singularity?
cues.zh: 黑洞的蒸发难道不会有点赶在 Alice 到达奇点之前发生吗？

cues.en: I don't really know if this is a question. It really is a request for evaporation.
cues.zh: 我都不确定这算不算个问题。这其实是在请求蒸发。

cues.en: SEAN: And the question is: don't you agree?
cues.zh: SEAN：问题是：你难道不同意吗？

cues.en: I do agree, actually you are completely right.
cues.zh: 我同意，实际上你完全正确。

cues.en: Your younger self was not right, because in a Black hole that would not have evaporated away,
cues.zh: 年轻时的你并不对，因为在一个还没蒸发掉的黑洞里，

cues.en: from Alice's point of view,
cues.zh: 从 Alice 的视角看，

cues.en: the clock is still ticking in an absolutely normal way,
cues.zh: 时钟仍以完全正常的方式走着，

cues.en: when she crosses the event horizon.
cues.zh: 当她穿过事件视界时。

cues.en: There is a finite number of seconds before she hits the singularity.
cues.zh: 她撞上奇点之前只剩有限的几秒。

cues.en: If the Black hole is one solar mass in size,
cues.zh: 如果这个黑洞只有一个太阳质量那么大，

cues.en: between the event horizon and the singularity, it takes about one millionth of a second from her point of view.
cues.zh: 从她的视角来看，从事件视界到奇点大约只需一百万分之一秒。

cues.en: But now with the Black hole evaporating, we honestly don't really have a very straight answer to that question.
cues.zh: 但如今黑洞在蒸发，说实话我们对这个问题并没有很明确的答案。

cues.en: There's still going to be tremendous gravitational fields in there.
cues.zh: 那里仍然会有极强的引力场。

cues.en: You are probably still going to be spaghettified,
cues.zh: 你大概还是会被拉成面条，

cues.en: but there is probably not a singularity. That is probably an artefact of classical general relativity.
cues.zh: 但那里可能并没有奇点。那可能只是经典广义相对论的产物。

cues.en: So it's more like you all get mixed up, and somehow your information comes out again.
cues.zh: 所以更像是你们全都被搅混了，而你的信息不知怎么又出来了。

cues.en: MAN: Would the Black hole not evaporate?
cues.zh: 男声：黑洞不会蒸发吗？

cues.en: From Bob's point of view, he's seen the Black hole evaporate, in external time.
cues.zh: 从Bob的视角看，在外部时间中，他已经看到黑洞蒸发了。

cues.en: Alice is almost frozen from his point of view,
cues.zh: 在他的视角里，Alice几乎是冻结的，

cues.en: so why isn't it that the Black hole evaporates before anything happens to Alice?
cues.zh: 那为什么不是黑洞在Alice身上发生任何事之前就蒸发了呢？

cues.en: It seems to tie in with your idea that
cues.zh: 这似乎和你的想法吻合，即

cues.en: the event horizon, which is this massive radiation, there's actually nothing inside.
cues.zh: 事件视界，也就是这巨大的辐射，里面其实什么都没有。

cues.en: SEAN: Well you know, Alice's point of view is also valid.
cues.zh: SEAN：嗯，你知道，Alice 的视角也是成立的。

cues.en: And in her point of view, she enters the event horizon.
cues.zh: 而在她的视角里，她进入了事件视界。

cues.en: The point is that, there is a tiny bit of exaggeration,
cues.zh: 关键在于，这有一点点夸张，

cues.en: when we say that from Bob's point of view, Alice stops moving.
cues.zh: 当我们说从 Bob 的视角看，Alice 停止运动时。

cues.en: If you see somebody, that means they are giving off radiation.
cues.zh: 如果你能看到某人，那就意味着他们在发出辐射。

cues.en: That means that time is passing.
cues.zh: 这意味着时间在流逝。

cues.en: So even though Bob sees Alice move more and more slowly,
cues.zh: 所以，尽管 Bob 看到 Alice 移动得越来越慢，

cues.en: Alice also appears redder and redder, and fainter and fainter
cues.zh: Alice 看上去也越来越红，越来越暗

cues.en: because she is embarrassed that she is falling into a Black hole,
cues.zh: 因为她为自己正掉进黑洞而感到尴尬，

cues.en: and because the photons are being red-shifted.
cues.zh: 也因为光子正在发生红移。

cues.en: Bob only gets a finite mount of information, about what happened to Alice,
cues.zh: Bob 只能获取关于 Alice 遭遇的有限信息，

cues.en: and that information is not complete.
cues.zh: 而且这些信息并不完整。

cues.en: The actual fact about Alice is that she enters into the Black hole.
cues.zh: 关于 Alice 的实际情况是，她进入了黑洞。

cues.en: MAN: Is there any potential research, aims and instrumentation
cues.zh: MAN：有没有什么潜在的研究、目标或观测手段，

cues.en: that could give you evidence about what you are talking about?
cues.zh: 能为你所说的内容提供证据？

cues.en: JENNIFER: Don't you love the theory? The pureness of the theory?
cues.zh: JENNIFER：你是不是特别喜欢理论？理论那种纯粹感？

cues.en: SEAN: yeah the theory should be enough!
cues.zh: SEAN：是啊，理论应该就够了！

cues.en: I think that the most we could possibly hope for is evidence of Hawking radiation.
cues.zh: 我觉得我们最多只能指望找到霍金辐射的证据。

cues.en: The evidence for Firewalls and crazy wormholes is a bit much to ask.
cues.zh: 至于防火墙和那些疯狂虫洞的证据，要求就有点太高了。

cues.en: If a Black hole is big, like if you make it from a star at the centre of a galaxy,
cues.zh: 如果黑洞很大，比如由星系中心的恒星形成，

cues.en: the weird thing about Black holes is that the bigger they are, the fainter they are,
cues.zh: 黑洞的奇怪之处在于：它们越大，反而越暗淡，

cues.en: the lower the temperature is.
cues.zh: 温度也越低。

cues.en: so for an astrophysical large Black hole, it's actually a lot colder than the surrounding space.
cues.zh: 所以对天体物理级别的大黑洞来说，它其实比周围空间冷得多。

cues.en: And the amount of Hawking radiation given off is a lot fainter than anything else in the universe.
cues.zh: 而它发出的霍金辐射，比宇宙中其他任何东西都微弱得多。

cues.en: The only hope is to find a really tiny Black hole, a primordial microscopic Black hole.
cues.zh: 唯一的希望是找到真正微小的黑洞，也就是原初的微观黑洞。

cues.en: and those could be exploding today.
cues.zh: 而它们可能正在今天爆炸。

cues.en: It's possible that we've been observing them in terms of gamma ray bursts or something like that.
cues.zh: 我们可能已经通过伽马射线暴之类的方式观测到它们了。

cues.en: It would just be very hard to tell whether or not you are actually observing an exploding Black hole,
cues.zh: 很难判断你观察到的到底是不是一个正在爆炸的黑洞，

cues.en: and probably there aren't any.
cues.zh: 而且很可能根本不存在。

cues.en: But that would be the biggest hope to find something.
cues.zh: 但那会是找到东西的最大希望。

cues.en: Actually Jennifer is an expert on the actual experiments in the lab for the Bill Andrews Black holes.
cues.zh: 其实 Jennifer 是实验室里 Bill Andrews 黑洞实际实验方面的专家。

cues.en: JENNIFER: Ohh. I am not an expert.
cues.zh: JENNIFER：哦，我不是专家。

cues.en: Expert is a strong word.
cues.zh: “专家”这个词有点太重了。

cues.en: Yes, there has small analogs that Bill Andrews was doing,
cues.zh: 是的，Bill Andrews 做过一些小型类似实验，

cues.en: using what's a little bit like water going down a drain.
cues.zh: 用的是有点像水流入下水道那样的方式。

cues.en: He is basically been able to create sonic analogs of Black holes, or with mechanical water waves
cues.zh: 他基本上已经能够制造出黑洞的声学类比物，或者用机械水波来做到这一点

cues.en: where you actually do get a kind of trapped effect similar to light not being able to escape,
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，你确实会得到一种被困住的效果，类似光无法逃逸

cues.en: suddenly sound can't escape.
cues.zh: 突然间，声音也逃不出去

cues.en: He's actually had a lot of very interesting hands-on experimental work with us.
cues.zh: 他实际上和我们做了很多非常有趣的动手实验工作

cues.en: The maths isn't exactly the same as for a Black hole,
cues.zh: 这里的数学并不完全等同于黑洞的数学

cues.en: but it's essentially what amounts to a toy model with some experimental evidence.
cues.zh: 但本质上，这相当于一个带有一些实验证据的玩具模型

cues.en: So the hope there is that through the small-scale experiments,
cues.zh: 所以希望在于，通过小尺度实验，

cues.en: they can actually get some insights into the larger full Black hole equations.
cues.zh: 他们能对更大尺度的完整黑洞方程获得一些洞见。

cues.en: SEAN: Yes.
cues.zh: SEAN：是的。

cues.en: MAN: I have two questions,
cues.zh: MAN：我有两个问题，

cues.en: both unrelated and related depending on your point of view.
cues.zh: 两者既无关又相关，取决于你的视角。

cues.en: The first question is that...SEAN: complementarity! MAN: Exactly.
cues.zh: 第一个问题是……SEAN：互补性！MAN：没错。

cues.en: So normal Black holes, supermassive, and these theoretical micro ones,
cues.zh: 那么普通黑洞、超大质量黑洞，以及这些理论上的微型黑洞，

cues.en: are they different sized animals of the same species
cues.zh: 它们是同一物种中不同体型的动物吗

cues.en: at least from a behaviour perspective?
cues.zh: 至少从行为角度来看？

cues.en: or is it different species? First question.
cues.zh: 还是不同的物种？这是第一个问题。

cues.en: Second: in terms of Bob and Carol and Ted and Alice,
cues.zh: 第二：就 Bob、Carol、Ted 和 Alice 而言，

cues.en: As far as information transfer, is there 100% fidelity of the conservation of information,
cues.zh: 就信息传递而言，信息守恒是否 100% 保真，

cues.en: or is there noise in the system?
cues.zh: 还是系统里存在噪声？

cues.en: SEAN: the first answer is that they are certainly the same species.
cues.zh: SEAN：第一个答案是，它们当然是同一物种。

cues.en: They are the same animal; in fact, Black holes are arguably the simplest things in the universe.
cues.zh: 它们是同一种动物；事实上，黑洞可以说是宇宙中最简单的东西。

cues.en: If you tell me what the mass of a Black hole is, what its electric charge is, and how fast it's spinning,
cues.zh: 如果你告诉我一个黑洞的质量、电荷以及自转速度，

cues.en: you have told me everything there is to know.
cues.zh: 那你就已经告诉我所有需要知道的信息了。

cues.en: It's not like a planet where you have to tell me the topography and what it's made of and all those things.
cues.zh: 它不像行星，不需要你告诉我地形、成分之类的所有细节。

cues.en: Black holes are all very simple and basically identical to each other.
cues.zh: 黑洞都非常简单，彼此基本一模一样。

cues.en: The information laws, you know, again we think an absolutely iron-clad rule of physics,
cues.zh: 信息定律嘛，我们仍然认为它是物理学中绝对不可动摇的规则，

cues.en: that information is 100% super-duper conserved.
cues.zh: 也就是信息是百分百、超级超级守恒的。

cues.en: It's like being a little bit pregnant, a little bit of information loss is very noticeable.
cues.zh: 这就像“有点怀孕”一样，哪怕一点点信息丢失都非常明显。

cues.en: We could be wrong about that, but that is the thought.
cues.zh: 我们可能想错了，但这就是我们的想法。

cues.en: That is the idea that we are working on.
cues.zh: 这就是我们正在研究的方向。

cues.en: JENNIFER: I think I would just add one thing, which is Black holes of different sizes actually radiate faster.
cues.zh: JENNIFER：我想补充一点：不同大小的黑洞，辐射速度其实有快慢之分。

cues.en: If they are smaller they disappear almost instantaneously.
cues.zh: 如果它们更小，就会几乎瞬间消失。

cues.en: If they are larger... So you know, the rate of which they evaporate is tied to their size,
cues.zh: 如果它们更大……所以你知道，它们蒸发的速度与大小有关，

cues.en: and that's the only difference. I mean, they are pretty much the same species
cues.zh: 这就是唯一的区别。我是说，它们基本上属于同一种类，

cues.en: but there are different size scales,
cues.zh: 但存在不同的大小尺度，

cues.en: and the does affect the rate of which they evaporate away.
cues.zh: 而这确实会影响它们蒸发殆尽的速度。

cues.en: SEAN: Someone right here had a question.
cues.zh: SEAN：这边有人有个问题。

cues.en: BOY: Thanks. That was a wonderful lecture.
cues.zh: BOY：谢谢。这堂课太精彩了。

cues.en: Going back to the holographic effect, if you end that door there...yeah that one...
cues.zh: 回到全息效应，如果你在那扇门那儿……对，就是那扇……

cues.en: and there's no space between you and the door,
cues.zh: 而且你和门之间没有空隙，

cues.en: what would happen to the information of the air between you and the door?
cues.zh: 那你和门之间空气的信息会怎样？

cues.en: SEAN: Well it's not...that's a very good question, but you have to understand exactly what's being said.
cues.zh: SEAN：嗯，这不是……这是个很好的问题，但你得准确理解这里说的是什么。

cues.en: If you think about a hologram, have you seen a hologram? BOY: Yeah.
cues.zh: 你想想全息图，你见过全息图吗？BOY：见过。

cues.en: So it's a two-dimensional piece of film that you shine light on and a three-dimensional image appears.
cues.zh: 它是一张二维的胶片，你往上面打光，就会出现三维图像。

cues.en: So the holographic principle is saying that this room is like that.
cues.zh: 全息原理说的就是，这个房间就像那样。

cues.en: So it's not saying that there's no air or no space in between me and the door.
cues.zh: 它并不是说我和门之间没有空气、没有空间。

cues.en: What it's saying that all of the information needed to talk about the air in between me and the door,
cues.zh: 它说的是，描述我和门之间空气所需的全部信息，

cues.en: is embedded in some secret invisible two-dimensional space.
cues.zh: 都嵌在某个隐秘而不可见的二维空间里。

cues.en: But it is all there.
cues.zh: 但一切都在里面。

cues.en: There are fewer ways that there could be air in between me and the door,
cues.zh: 我和门之间能出现空气的方式更少，

cues.en: than you might have thought,
cues.zh: 比你想象的还要少，

cues.en: because there isn't as much room in the two-dimensional hologram to put them
cues.zh: 因为二维全息图里能容纳这些方式的空间没那么多，

cues.en: as there would be in a three-dimensional space.
cues.zh: 不像三维空间里那么多。

cues.en: BOY: Thanks.
cues.zh: 男孩：谢谢。

cues.en: MAN: This follows on, actually from talking about this principle of two-dimensional space,
cues.zh: 男人：这其实承接了刚才讲的二维空间原理，

cues.en: in which three-dimensional information is encoded.
cues.zh: 三维信息就编码在这种空间里。

cues.en: I just wondered if you could talk about how this relates to the prediction of the string theory,
cues.zh: 我想知道，你能不能谈谈这和弦理论的预言有什么关系，

cues.en: which predicts a lot more dimensions, I believe,
cues.zh: 我相信它预言了多得多的维度，

cues.en: and what we actually mean by dimensions in both circumstances.
cues.zh: 以及在这两种情况下，我们说的维度到底指什么。

cues.en: JENNIFER: That's on you. SEAN: Yeah, you would think that they would get their story straight,
cues.zh: JENNIFER：这得怪你。SEAN：是啊，你会以为他们总该把说法统一一下，

cues.en: and decide whether there are more or fewer dimensions than we thought there were.
cues.zh: 并确定维度到底比我们以为的更多还是更少。

cues.en: But it's actually quite compatible.
cues.zh: 但这其实相当兼容。

cues.en: In the string theory, there are supposed to be extra dimensions of space,
cues.zh: 在弦论中，应该存在额外的空间维度，

cues.en: which are invisible to us for a completely different reason.
cues.zh: 它们对我们不可见的原因则完全不同。

cues.en: Those dimensions are invisible to us because they are curled up, into a little tiny ball,
cues.zh: 那些维度之所以不可见，是因为它们卷曲成了一个小球，

cues.en: and we can't see them; they are much smaller than atoms,
cues.zh: 我们看不到它们；它们比原子小得多，

cues.en: OR we are stuck on some three-dimensional surface inside some bigger space and we just literally can't get there.
cues.zh: 或者我们被困在某个更大空间里的某个三维表面上，真的就是到不了那里。

cues.en: This is saying that, all of those descriptions are ways of talking about curved space-time,
cues.zh: 这是说，所有这些描述都是在谈论弯曲时空的方式，

cues.en: but the right way to talk about the fundamental nature in curved space-time
cues.zh: 但要谈论弯曲时空中的根本本质，正确的方式

cues.en: is just to go one dimension less.
cues.zh: 就是少用一个维度。

cues.en: So however many dimensions there really are, in the fundamental description of reality,
cues.zh: 所以，无论现实的基本描述中真正有多少个维度，

cues.en: curved space-time with gravity always appears like it has one dimension more.
cues.zh: 带引力的弯曲时空总是显得多出一个维度。

cues.en: That seems to be the principle that holography works on.
cues.zh: 这似乎就是全息术所依据的原理。

cues.en: So it might be that the real number of dimensions of space-time is eight,
cues.zh: 所以，时空的真实维数也许是八维，

cues.en: and therefore gravity works in nine-dimensional space-time; that's one of the theories you can write about.
cues.zh: 因此引力在九维时空中起作用；这是你可以写的一种理论。

cues.en: MAN: is there any suggestion that there is a link
cues.zh: MAN：有没有任何说法认为，存在一种联系

cues.en: between quantum gravity and dark energy or dark matter?
cues.zh: 存在于量子引力与暗能量或暗物质之间？

cues.en: SEAN: Any question that begins with "is there a suggestion", the answer is Yes.
cues.zh: SEAN：任何以“有没有人提出”开头的问题，答案都是肯定的。

cues.en: People have suggested that.
cues.zh: 人们确实提出过这种说法。

cues.en: Dark matter is probably quite parochial and conventional by these terms.
cues.zh: 按这些说法，暗物质大概相当局限，也相当常规。

cues.en: It's probably just another particle that we haven't found yet.
cues.zh: 它可能只是另一种我们还没发现的粒子。

cues.en: People have tried more outlandish ideas: it' a modification of gravity; something holographic,
cues.zh: 人们还尝试过更离谱的想法：比如对引力的修改；某种全息式的解释，

cues.en: something like that.
cues.zh: 诸如此类。

cues.en: Those ideas literally don't fit the data very well.
cues.zh: 这些想法其实都和数据吻合得不太好。

cues.en: Whereas the idea that dark matter is just another particle seems to fit the data very well.
cues.zh: 而暗物质只是另一种粒子这个想法，似乎和数据吻合得非常好。

cues.en: Dark energy, which is more subtle, it's something that is smoothly distributed throughout the universe,
cues.zh: 暗能量则更微妙，它均匀地弥漫在整个宇宙中，

cues.en: and makes the universe accelerate.
cues.zh: 并让宇宙加速膨胀。

cues.en: We have less idea where the origin of that is, so it's absolutely possible that when we do,
cues.zh: 我们对它的起源更不清楚，所以当我们做到时，完全有可能，

cues.en: it will in some way involve ideas like holography,
cues.zh: 它会以某种方式涉及全息术之类的想法，

cues.en: but I really can't tell you precisely how.
cues.zh: 但我真的没法确切告诉你具体如何。

cues.en: SEAN: Right there.
cues.zh: SEAN：就在那里。

cues.en: MAN: Hi, you spoke already about how quantising gravity
cues.zh: MAN：你好，你之前已经谈到引力量子化

cues.en: was one of the greatest challenges in modern physics.
cues.zh: 是现代物理学中最大的挑战之一。

cues.en: Could you comment on how cosmic inflation helps explain that?
cues.zh: 你能谈谈宇宙暴胀如何帮助解释这一点吗？

cues.en: SEAN: Don't think it does, is the short answer.
cues.zh: SEAN：简短的回答是，我不认为它能解释。

cues.en: But it might help us learn something about what works.
cues.zh: 但这可能有助于我们了解哪些方法有效。

cues.en: so inflation is this idea that in the first, a very very tiny fraction a second after the Big Bang,
cues.zh: 所以暴胀这个想法是：在大爆炸之后极短的一瞬间，

cues.en: the universe underwent a huge fast amount of expansion that smoothed everything out,
cues.zh: 宇宙经历了一场巨大而快速的膨胀，把一切变得平滑，

cues.en: and left us with the universe we see today.
cues.zh: 并留下了我们今天所见的宇宙。

cues.en: The models that we have of inflation are basically classical,
cues.zh: 我们现有的暴胀模型基本上都是经典的，

cues.en: are basically not involving quantum gravity.
cues.zh: 基本上都不涉及量子引力。

cues.en: There is a little bit of quantum field theory in there, but gravity is still classical in that regime.
cues.zh: 里面有一点点量子场论，但在那种情形下引力仍然是经典的。

cues.en: So you don't need quantum gravity to make inflation work, nor does inflation rely on quantum gravity in any way.
cues.zh: 所以，不需要量子引力也能让暴胀成立，暴胀也完全不依赖量子引力。

cues.en: However, if inflation is real and we can get observational evidence about it,
cues.zh: 不过，如果暴胀是真实的，而且我们能得到关于它的观测证据，

cues.en: it is a phenomenon that happens at an energy scale much closer to the energy scales of quantum gravity
cues.zh: 那么它是一种发生在远更接近量子引力能标的能量尺度上的现象，

cues.en: than any other phenomenon that we have any way to observe in the universe today.
cues.zh: 比我们今天在宇宙中有任何办法观测到的其他任何现象都更接近。

cues.en: So literally the difference in energy between the temperature of the air in this room,
cues.zh: 所以，说白了，这个房间里空气温度所对应的能量，

cues.en: and the protons that you smash together at the LHC, the Large Hadron Collider,
cues.zh: 和你在 LHC，也就是大型强子对撞机里对撞的质子之间的能量差，

cues.en: is less than the difference in energy between those large hadron collider protons and the inflation energy.
cues.zh: 还小于那些大型强子对撞机质子和暴胀能量之间的能量差。

cues.en: So if we can make that leap up to inflation, which maybe we have with recent data about microwave background,
cues.zh: 所以，如果我们能跃升到暴胀阶段，或许最近的微波背景数据已经让我们做到了，

cues.en: that's as much of a leap forward in energy as all of the previous rest of the history of physics.
cues.zh: 那在能量尺度上的跨越，相当于此前整个物理学史所有进展的总和。

cues.en: SEAN: This side. Do we have any...ah good.
cues.zh: SEAN：这边。有没有……啊，好。

cues.en: MAN: Hi, thanks again for the talk. Fantastic.
cues.zh: 男士：你好，再次感谢你的演讲。非常精彩。

cues.en: I wanted to ask, would you comment on what these paradoxes might mean
cues.zh: 我想问，能否请你谈谈这些悖论可能意味着什么，

cues.en: for our understanding of cosmology in the sense of the origin of the universe, and its future.
cues.zh: 对于我们理解宇宙学——也就是宇宙的起源和它的未来——意味着什么。

cues.en: In particular, I think I remember reading that holography may link what we think of eteranl inflation
cues.zh: 特别是，我想我记得读到过，全息术可能把我们所说的永恒暴胀

cues.en: and the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 与量子力学的多世界诠释联系起来。

cues.en: What we think are completely different things,
cues.zh: 我们以为完全不同的东西，

cues.en: are somehow linked via holography, but no idea if I got that right, or How.
cues.zh: 不知怎么通过全息术联系了起来，但我不知道我是否理解对了，也不知道是怎么联系起来的。

cues.en: SEAN: Yeah, you do actually have that right.
cues.zh: SEAN：是的，你确实说对了。

cues.en: So, complementarity. The question is, what is this thing got to do with cosmology?
cues.zh: 所以，互补性。问题是，这东西和宇宙学有什么关系？

cues.en: It's interesting, because as a cosmologist, my goal in choosing my career was
cues.zh: 有趣的是，作为一名宇宙学家，我选择职业的目标曾是

cues.en: to go into the simplest possible area of science, cos the universe is actually very simple.
cues.zh: 进入尽可能最简单的科学领域，因为宇宙其实非常简单。

cues.en: You ignore all the details and just look at it on large scales.
cues.zh: 你忽略所有细节，只看大尺度上的它。

cues.en: And yet, I went wrong, because Black hole are actually even simpler than the universe
cues.zh: 但我错了，因为黑洞其实比宇宙还简单。

cues.en: So applying these ideas to cosmology is hard, cos the universe can do more things than a Black hole can do.
cues.zh: 所以把这些想法应用到宇宙学很难，因为宇宙能做的事比黑洞更多。

cues.en: It's like that question; Black holes just can't do many...there is just not that many possible Black holes.
cues.zh: 这就像那个问题：黑洞就是做不了多少事……可能存在的黑洞并没有那么多。

cues.en: Having said that, let's imagine taking complementarity very very seriously.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，我们不妨设想一下，非常非常认真地对待互补性。

cues.en: Complementarity says that the point of view of someone outside the horizon is different than someone inside the horizon.
cues.zh: 互补性认为，视界外的人与视界内的人，视角是不同的。

cues.en: So because our universe is accelerating out, because there is dark energy,
cues.zh: 所以，由于我们的宇宙在加速膨胀，由于存在暗能量，

cues.en: there is a different kind a horizon that we are inside.
cues.zh: 存在着一种不同的视界，而我们正处在它内部。

cues.en: If distant galaxies move far enough away, they are accelerated away by the expansion of the universe
cues.zh: 如果遥远星系移动得足够远，它们就会被宇宙膨胀加速推离

cues.en: and we will never see them again.
cues.zh: 我们就再也看不到它们了。

cues.en: So they are outside the horizon.
cues.zh: 所以它们位于视界之外。

cues.en: So certain ambitious physicists have said, that maybe there is this certain complementarity
cues.zh: 于是，一些雄心勃勃的物理学家说过，也许存在某种互补性

cues.en: that works for cosmological horizons,
cues.zh: 它适用于宇宙学视界，

cues.en: as well as Black hole horizons.
cues.zh: 也适用于黑洞视界。

cues.en: And if that were to be true, what we will be saying is that, the entire description of the universe,
cues.zh: 如果真是这样，我们要说的就是，对整个宇宙的描述，

cues.en: is our observable universe plus our horizon.
cues.zh: 就是我们的可观测宇宙加上我们的视界。

cues.en: Everything outside is secretly embedded on our horizon.
cues.zh: 外部的一切都暗中嵌入在我们的视界之中。

cues.en: So you don't need to talk about the entire universe outside of what we can see.
cues.zh: 所以你不需要讨论可见范围之外的整个宇宙。

cues.en: It's all secretly encoded in this local bit.
cues.zh: 这一切都秘密编码在这个局部比特中。

cues.en: OK.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And if that's true, then quantum mechanics says the universe is like any other quantum mechanical system,
cues.zh: 如果这是真的，那么量子力学认为，宇宙就像任何其他量子力学系统一样，

cues.en: it can be a superposition of different possibilities.
cues.zh: 它可以是不同可能性的叠加态。

cues.en: So this observable bit of universe can be a superposition of different states of being.
cues.zh: 所以，宇宙中这个可观测的比特可以是不同存在状态的叠加。

cues.en: and that would be the cosmological multiverse.
cues.zh: 那就是宇宙学多元宇宙。

cues.en: So the many-worlds in quantum mechanics and the cosmological multiverse would be brought together
cues.zh: 所以量子力学中的多世界和宇宙学多元宇宙会被结合在一起

cues.en: in a happy relationship, and it's all completely speculative at this point.
cues.zh: 和谐共处，不过目前这完全是推测。

cues.en: JENNIFER: Is there one up there?
cues.zh: JENNIFER：上面有人吗？

cues.en: SEAN: I haven't seen any up there but there are a couple of plucky folks over here.
cues.zh: SEAN：我在上面没看到人，不过这边有几位挺有胆量的人。

cues.en: Is there anyone up there?
cues.zh: 上面有人吗？

cues.en: MAN: I just wanted to talk about dark energy and inflation.
cues.zh: MAN：我只是想谈谈暗能量和暴胀。

cues.en: If you imagine a speedboat going across water, and the speedboat itself is inflation,
cues.zh: 如果你想象一艘快艇划过水面，而快艇本身就是暴胀，

cues.en: the ripples behind it might be dark energy,
cues.zh: 它身后的波纹可能就是暗能量，

cues.en: because dark energy says that things that are furthest away from us are moving further away fastest,
cues.zh: 因为暗能量说的是，离我们最远的东西正在以最快的速度远离我们，

cues.en: and those that are closest to us are moving away less quickly.
cues.zh: 而离我们最近的东西远离得没那么快。

cues.en: So that would be the same thing with the speedboat, with the ripples coming out from the speedboat.
cues.zh: 所以快艇也是同样的道理，波纹从快艇向外扩散。

cues.en: As you get further away from the actual speedboat, the ripples themselves move slower.
cues.zh: 当你离实际那艘快艇越远，波纹本身移动得越慢。

cues.en: So are we looking for something that doesn't actually exist? It's just inflation.
cues.zh: 所以，我们是在寻找一个实际上并不存在的东西吗？那只是暴胀。

cues.en: SEAN: So, my personal point of view is that the speedboat analogy is probably not the best one,
cues.zh: SEAN：所以，我个人认为，快艇这个类比可能不是最合适的，

cues.en: because inflation is not the movement of something through something else.
cues.zh: 因为暴胀并不是某物穿过另一物的运动。

cues.en: It is literally the size of the universe changing with time.
cues.zh: 它实际上就是宇宙的尺度随时间变化。

cues.en: It is true that when we talk about the acceleration of the universe and dark energy,
cues.zh: 确实，当我们谈论宇宙加速膨胀和暗能量时，

cues.en: distant galaxies are moving away from us faster than nearby galaxies.
cues.zh: 遥远星系远离我们的速度比近处星系更快。

cues.en: But that's only because the universe is expanding.
cues.zh: 但这只是因为宇宙在膨胀。

cues.en: That was still true even before we knew about dark energy or the acceleration of the universe.
cues.zh: 甚至在我们了解暗能量或宇宙加速膨胀之前，这一点就已经成立了。

cues.en: Edwin Hubble's famous law says that the apparent velocity of a galaxy,
cues.zh: Edwin Hubble 的著名定律指出，一个星系的视速度，

cues.en: is its distant times a constant called the Hubble's constant.
cues.zh: 等于它的距离乘以一个常数，叫做哈勃常数。

cues.en: So as the distant gets bigger, the apparent velocity gets bigger and bigger.
cues.zh: 所以距离越大，视速度就越来越大。

cues.en: That's really just explained by the fact that there is more space,
cues.zh: 这其实只是因为在你和那个遥远天体之间，

cues.en: in between you and the distant thing.
cues.zh: 有更多的空间。

cues.en: So, it's a tricky thing, because we very naturally fall back on analogies,
cues.zh: 所以这事很棘手，因为我们很自然地会借助类比，

cues.en: that relate what the universe is doing to things that we are familiar with,
cues.zh: 把宇宙正在做的事，和我们熟悉的事物联系起来，

cues.en: all of which are things inside the universe, doing things, subsets of the universe doing things.
cues.zh: 而这些事物全都是宇宙内部的东西，在做事，是宇宙的子集在做事。

cues.en: But in some ways, the universe is a unique kind of beast.
cues.zh: 但从某些方面说，宇宙是一种独一无二的奇特存在。

cues.en: I think that dark energy really needs to be some kind of energy.
cues.zh: 我认为暗能量确实必须是某种能量。

cues.en: I don't think it's sort of automatic or anything like that.
cues.zh: 我不认为它是某种自动产生的东西，或者诸如此类。

cues.en: MAN: Sure.
cues.zh: MAN：当然。

cues.en: MAN: Thank you. I'm still having a little trouble understanding what you were saying when...
cues.zh: MAN：谢谢。我还是有点没太理解你刚才说的，当……

cues.en: SEAN: What?
cues.zh: SEAN：什么？

cues.en: Alright...
cues.zh: 好吧……

cues.en: MAN: Back early on with you Alice photon falling into the Black hole, and your Bob photon being emitted.
cues.zh: MAN：回到早先，你那个 Alice 光子掉进黑洞，而你的 Bob 光子被发射出来。

cues.en: Why is it that Bob is emitted? Why can't he just hang around outside the event horizon for a little while,
cues.zh: 为什么 Bob 会被发射出去？他为什么不能先在事件视界外待一会儿，

cues.en: and then follow Alice in just a little bit later?
cues.zh: 然后稍晚一点再跟着 Alice 进去？

cues.en: And sort of following on from that,
cues.zh: 顺着这个再说，

cues.en: I also don't quite see where this Firewall comes from.
cues.zh: 我也不太明白这个防火墙是从哪来的。

cues.en: Does that come from the same phenomenon as the original Hawking radiation?
cues.zh: 这跟最初的霍金辐射是同一个现象吗？

cues.en: Or is that just something else that would give us a similar prediction?
cues.zh: 还是说那只是另一种会给出类似预测的东西？

cues.en: SEAN: So to the first question, why couldn't Bob just hang out?
cues.zh: SEAN：那么回到第一个问题，Bob 为什么不能就待在那儿？

cues.en: Have you ever tried hanging out right next to the event horizon of a Black hole?
cues.zh: 你有没有试过就在黑洞事件视界旁边待着？

cues.en: I thinks as Jennifer mentioned, most of the virtual particles near the event horizon do just stay there.
cues.zh: 我觉得，就像 Jennifer 提到的，事件视界附近的大多数虚拟粒子确实就留在那里。

cues.en: They get created and they get annihilated very quickly; they don't escape to infinity.
cues.zh: 它们很快产生又很快湮灭；不会逃到无穷远。

cues.en: So when we draw these pictures, we are just picking out the plucky ones that manage to escape.
cues.zh: 所以画这些图时，我们只是挑出那些侥幸逃脱的粒子。

cues.en: So most of the virtual particles are just sitting there near the horizon.
cues.zh: 所以大多数虚粒子只是待在视界附近。

cues.en: The important thing about those particles is that,
cues.zh: 这些粒子的关键在于，

cues.en: if the combination of the states of all those particles looks like empty space,
cues.zh: 如果所有这些粒子的状态组合起来看起来像空无一物的空间，

cues.en: it must be that all those particles are entangled with each other,
cues.zh: 那么所有这些粒子必定彼此纠缠，

cues.en: in a very intricate way, in a very intimate way I should say.
cues.zh: 以一种极其复杂、我该说极其紧密的方式。

cues.en: The Firewall paradox is just saying that,
cues.zh: 火墙悖论只是在说，

cues.en: if you want to get the information out
cues.zh: 如果你想获取信息，

cues.en: from Bob and all the other particles coming on later,
cues.zh: 从 Bob 以及之后到来的所有其他粒子那里，

cues.en: then it can't be true that Bob and Alice are entangled at the same time.
cues.zh: 那么 Bob 和 Alice 同时处于纠缠状态就不可能成立。

cues.en: If Bob is entangled with Alice, he is not entangled with anything else,
cues.zh: 如果 Bob 和 Alice 纠缠，他就不会和其他任何东西纠缠，

cues.en: and therefore the information is getting lost every time he leaves.
cues.zh: 因此每次他离开时，信息都在丢失。

cues.en: But as soon as you disentangle Alice and Bob down there,
cues.zh: 但一旦你在下面把 Alice 和 Bob 解除纠缠，

cues.en: it's no longer empty space.
cues.zh: 它就不再是空无一物的空间了。

cues.en: It's a wall of high energy particles.
cues.zh: 那是一堵由高能粒子组成的墙。

cues.en: That's the Firewall claim in a nutshell.
cues.zh: 一句话概括，这就是火墙假说。

cues.en: JENNIFER: Finally someone back here.
cues.zh: 珍妮弗：终于有人到后面来了。

cues.en: MAN: Yeah, sorry...OK so just another question relating vaguely to entanglement,
cues.zh: 男：是啊，抱歉……好，我再问一个跟纠缠隐约沾边的问题，

cues.en: and I'm sorry if this was covered in the lecture and I maybe dropped off and missed it.
cues.zh: 如果讲座里讲过、而我走神错过了，那很抱歉。

cues.en: It was very interesting. That could be the beer I had earlier.
cues.zh: 讲得很有意思。也可能是我之前喝的啤酒起了作用。

cues.en: So when you talk about entanglement,
cues.zh: 那么当您谈到纠缠时，

cues.en: in my mind, that is a way of you describing a supposition, which is a way of you saying that
cues.zh: 在我看来，那是您在描述一种假设，也就是在说

cues.en: something you observe infers the truth about something else.
cues.zh: 你观测到的某样东西，能推断出另一样东西的真相。

cues.en: So for example, if you observe that the ball is blue,
cues.zh: 例如，如果你观察到这个球是蓝色的，

cues.en: that implies that the other ball is red.
cues.zh: 那就意味着另一个球是红色的。

cues.en: But regardless of whether you observe one truth or another truth,
cues.zh: 但无论你观察到的是哪一个事实，

cues.en: both of those truths still exist, whether you observe them or not.
cues.zh: 这两个事实都仍然存在，无论你观察与否。

cues.en: so a ball is still blue and a ball is still red, somewhere.
cues.zh: 所以某个地方仍然有一个蓝球和一个红球。

cues.en: So as soon as you observe whether one ball is blue or red or whatever,
cues.zh: 因此，一旦你观察到某个球是蓝的、红的还是别的什么，

cues.en: then that entanglement, in a way, does that cease to exist?
cues.zh: 那么这种纠缠，在某种意义上，是不是就不复存在了？

cues.en: Because you observed that one ball is red,
cues.zh: 因为你观察到其中一个球是红色的，

cues.en: the other ball becomes blue; they are entangled.
cues.zh: 另一个球就变成蓝色；它们处于纠缠状态。

cues.en: But does that relationship maintain, so if you were able to change the ball you have observed to red,
cues.zh: 但这种关系会维持吗？那如果你能把你观测到的那颗球改成红色，

cues.en: does the other one become blue?
cues.zh: 另一个球会变成蓝色吗？

cues.en: Or does that entanglement cease at some point of observation?
cues.zh: 还是这种纠缠会在某个观测时刻停止？

cues.en: This is kind of my question.
cues.zh: 这算是我的问题。

cues.en: I don't know if that makes sense.
cues.zh: 我不知道这是否说得通。

cues.en: SEAN: It is a perfectly good question, and there are two things.
cues.zh: SEAN：这是个非常好的问题，有两点。

cues.en: One is that, yes the entanglement does persist.
cues.zh: 第一点是，是的，纠缠确实会持续存在。

cues.en: When you observe one box, or one ball, the entanglement that was there, stays there.
cues.zh: 当你观察一个盒子，或者一个球时，原本存在的纠缠仍然留在那里。

cues.en: So one way to be entangled is,
cues.zh: 所以一种处于纠缠态的方式是，

cues.en: this ball is definitely red, and this ball is definitely blue.
cues.zh: 这个球确定是红色，这个球确定是蓝色。

cues.en: It's a kind of entanglement.
cues.zh: 这是一种纠缠。

cues.en: More interestingly, there is a fraction of the superposition that is red and blue,
cues.zh: 更有意思的是，叠加态中有一部分是红蓝组合，

cues.en: and the opposite that is blue and red over here.
cues.zh: 而这里相反的一部分是蓝红组合。

cues.en: But the point is when you make an observation and make this one red,
cues.zh: 但关键是，当你进行观察并让这个球变成红色时，

cues.en: that one instantly becomes blue.
cues.zh: 那个球会瞬间变成蓝色。

cues.en: They are still entangled, just in a more trivial way.
cues.zh: 它们仍然处于纠缠态，只是方式更简单了。

cues.en: And that is an experimental fact.
cues.zh: 这是实验事实。

cues.en: That is not just a theory; we have done that experiment.
cues.zh: 这不只是理论；我们做过那个实验。

cues.en: We have put them in superpositions, move them apart and observe them,
cues.zh: 我们把它们置于叠加态，把它们分开再观察，

cues.en: and then checked, and it always works out exactly as we predicted.
cues.zh: 然后检查，结果总是和我们预测的完全一致。

cues.en: MAN: So can you then sort of reboot the supposition with the same two particles?
cues.zh: MAN：那你能不能用同样两个粒子把叠加态重置一下？

cues.en: SEAN: You can...once have observed the particle and you have seen that it's red or blue,
cues.zh: SEAN：可以……一旦观察过这个粒子，看到它是红色还是蓝色，

cues.en: it stays red or blue. So that is what's called collapse of the wave function, in quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 它就会保持红色或蓝色。这就是量子力学中所谓的波函数坍缩。

cues.en: and it's very mysterious, collapse of the wave function.
cues.zh: 这非常神秘，波函数坍缩。

cues.en: Before you saw, it was in a superposition,
cues.zh: 在你观察之前，它处于叠加态，

cues.en: afterward, it's one or the other,
cues.zh: 观察之后，它就只能是其中一个，

cues.en: and that's what it's going to be from now on.
cues.zh: 从此以后都会如此。

cues.en: You have come very close to inventing what is called many worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics,
cues.zh: 你差点就发明了所谓的量子力学多世界诠释，

cues.en: which says that, MAN: Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 它认为，男子：非常感谢。

cues.en: SEAN: when I...You are late!
cues.zh: SEAN：当我……你来晚了！

cues.en: MAN: I'll take that. I'll call or text my mom. She'd be very proud.
cues.zh: 男子：这个我收下了。我会给我妈打电话或发短信。她会非常骄傲。

cues.en: JENNIFER: about a hundred years too late.
cues.zh: JENNIFER：大概晚了一百年吧。

cues.en: SEAN: A little bit too late, and the guy who invented it kind of went crazy.
cues.zh: SEAN：确实有点太晚了，而且发明它的人后来有点疯了。

cues.en: Hugh Everett, who invented the many-worlds interpretation,
cues.zh: Hugh Everett 提出了多世界诠释，

cues.en: said look, when you talk about these experiments, you have to realise that
cues.zh: 他说，你看，当你讨论这些实验时，必须意识到

cues.en: you, a human being are made of quantum mechanical particle,
cues.zh: 你，作为一个人，是由量子力学粒子构成的，

cues.en: so you obey the rules of quantum mechanics.
cues.zh: 所以你也遵循量子力学的规律。

cues.en: You have a quantum state that can be in superposition.
cues.zh: 你有一个可以处于叠加态的量子态。

cues.en: When you open the box, and look to see if the box if red or blue,
cues.zh: 当你打开盒子，看里面是红色还是蓝色时，

cues.en: it's not that you see it red, and the blueness disappears, or vice versa.
cues.zh: 并不是你看到它是红色，蓝色就消失了，反之亦然。

cues.en: It's that you evolve into a superposition of the ball was red and you saw it red,
cues.zh: 而是你演化成“球是红色且你看到红色”的叠加态，

cues.en: plus the ball was blue and you saw it blue.
cues.zh: 再加上“球是蓝色且你看到蓝色”。

cues.en: There are now two different copies of the world in which you saw different things going on.
cues.zh: 现在有两个不同的世界副本，你在其中看到不同的事情发生。

cues.en: They are both equally real, and they will never communicate with each other ever again.
cues.zh: 它们同样真实，而且彼此再也不会通信。

cues.en: They are for all intensive purposes, separate worlds,
cues.zh: 实际上，它们是彼此分离的世界，

cues.en: multiple worlds in reality.
cues.zh: 现实中存在多个世界。

cues.en: If you believe that, which I do actually, I think that it's probably true,
cues.zh: 如果你相信这一点——我确实相信——我认为这很可能是真的，

cues.en: you should go to the APP store and download something called universe splitter.
cues.zh: 你应该去 App Store 下载一个叫 Universe Splitter 的东西。

cues.en: It is an iPhone APP, where it gives you two options and you can say,
cues.zh: 它是一个 iPhone 应用，会给你两个选项，你可以说，

cues.en: I would like to study physics in graduate school, or study philosophy in graduate school.
cues.zh: 我想在研究生院学物理，或者学哲学。

cues.en: It will send a signal to a lab that sends a photon and splits it then observe it,
cues.zh: 它会向一个实验室发送信号，实验室发出一个光子并把它分束，然后观测它，

cues.en: and it comes back and tells you which branch of the wave function of the universe you are in,
cues.zh: 然后它回来告诉你，你处在宇宙波函数的哪个分支上，

cues.en: and you should o study philosophy.
cues.zh: 而你应该去学哲学。

cues.en: And if you promise you'd do what the phone tells you to do,
cues.zh: 如果你保证会照手机说的去做，

cues.en: there is another branch of reality in which you became a physicist.
cues.zh: 那么在现实的另一个分支里，你就成了物理学家。

cues.en: MAN: And when do I go on the X-factor... SEAN: That's right!
cues.zh: 男：那我什么时候上《X-factor》……SEAN：没错！

cues.en: MAN: Thank you!
cues.zh: 男：谢谢！

cues.en: SEAN: One more question, good right in the middle right there. You can just move it right there.
cues.zh: SEAN：再问一个问题，好，就放正中间那儿。你把它移到那儿就行。

cues.en: WOMAN: I read earlier this year that Stephen Hawking , I think, probably in connection with the Firewall,
cues.zh: 女：今年早些时候我读到，Stephen Hawking，我想，可能和火墙有关，

cues.en: wrote an issue, with saying something about maybe Black holes didn't exist,
cues.zh: 写了一篇文章，说也许黑洞并不存在，

cues.en: as such as having an event horizon.
cues.zh: 严格来说并不是拥有事件视界的那种。

cues.en: and maybe had more of an apparent horizon instead.
cues.zh: 而可能更多是一个表观视界。

cues.en: Can you sort of say a bit about that? Sort of explain it a bit, sort of how it adds to the debate?
cues.zh: 你能稍微谈谈这个吗？稍微解释一下，它是怎么加入这场争论的？

cues.en: JENNIFER: Well I can say something as a science writer, that the new covered was terrible of that.
cues.zh: JENNIFER：作为科学作家，我可以说，关于那件事的新闻报道很糟糕。

cues.en: That's actually not what he said.
cues.zh: 其实那不是他说的。

cues.en: The headlines and some of the covers of that were not very good, I think,
cues.zh: 我觉得，那些标题和其中一些封面并不太好，

cues.en: really hadn't looked very deeply into what Hawking was actually saying.
cues.zh: 其实并没有深入探究 Hawking 到底在说什么。

cues.en: If you ask Sean, Sean will tell you that he thinks Hawking is possibly not correct.
cues.zh: 如果你问 Sean，Sean 会告诉你，他觉得 Hawking 可能不对。

cues.en: I will let you elaborate. SEAN: It's one of the few times in my life,
cues.zh: 我让你详细说说。SEAN：这是我人生中少有的几次，

cues.en: where I thought to myself: of course Stephen Hawking.
cues.zh: 我心里想：当然是 Stephen Hawking。

cues.en: Because he wrote this paper, and it was really just a conference proceedings.
cues.zh: 因为他写了这篇论文，而它其实只是一篇会议论文。

cues.en: He had given a talk, and he typed it up in his computer
cues.zh: 他做过一个演讲，然后在电脑上把它打了出来

cues.en: And he ended it off. It was very short; there were no details, no equations.
cues.zh: 然后就收尾了。文章很短，没有细节，也没有公式。

cues.en: it was just like a suggestion.
cues.zh: 那其实只是个提议。

cues.en: But because his name is Stephen Hawking, and he's done amazingly wonderful things in the history of physics,
cues.zh: 但因为他的名字是 Stephen Hawking，而且他在物理学史上做出了极其了不起的成就，

cues.en: and everyone pays attention to him,
cues.zh: 所有人都关注他，

cues.en: people latched onto it, and there is this one sentence in his paper, which says that:
cues.zh: 人们就抓住这个说法不放，而且他论文里有一句话是这么说的：

cues.en: Therefore, Black holes do not exist in the sense that blablabla. instead, they exist in this sense.
cues.zh: 因此，黑洞在 bla bla bla 的意义上并不存在；相反，它们是在这个意义上存在的。

cues.en: And the headline in Nature the next day was
cues.zh: 第二天《Nature》的标题是

cues.en: Stephen Hawking thinks that Black holes do not exist.
cues.zh: Stephen Hawking 认为黑洞不存在。

cues.en: So, if you go back the picture Jennifer showed of the centre of our galaxy,
cues.zh: 回到Jennifer展示的银河系中心那张图，

cues.en: remember, this is data.
cues.zh: 记住，这是数据。

cues.en: The orbits of these stars that are plotted here; it's done in a computer program,
cues.zh: 这里画出的这些恒星轨道，是用计算机程序做出来的，

cues.en: but they are based on observations of the stars,
cues.zh: 但它们基于对这些恒星的观测，

cues.en: around a big plus sign.
cues.zh: 围绕着一个大加号。

cues.en: If you believe, it's a Black hole,
cues.zh: 如果你相信的话，那是一个黑洞，

cues.en: because it's enormously massive and enormously small and enormously dark.
cues.zh: 因为它质量极大、体积极小，而且极其黑暗。

cues.en: And Stephen Hawking, if you asked him: is there is Black hole in the centre of our galaxy? He would say yes.
cues.zh: 而Stephen Hawking，如果你问他：我们银河系中心有黑洞吗？他会说有。

cues.en: So I think that, he is gesturing in the direction of
cues.zh: 所以我认为，他正朝着某个方向示意，

cues.en: a certain kind of resolution of the Black hole Firewalls problem,
cues.zh: 某种解决黑洞防火墙问题的方案，

cues.en: to take the idea of an event horizon a little bit less seriously, given that Black holes eventually evaporate.
cues.zh: 也就是，鉴于黑洞最终会蒸发，不必把事件视界的概念看得那么认真。

cues.en: But there is a long way to go before enough meat is put on those bones to call it even a proposal,
cues.zh: 但要把这些想法充实到足以称为一个提案，还有很长的路要走，

cues.en: much less a theory.
cues.zh: 更不用说成为一个理论了。

cues.en: And I think I'm being told that we are out of space and time, so we will...
cues.zh: 而且我想有人提醒我，我们没时间也没空间了，所以我们会……

cues.en: we have come to the end of space-time; thank you once again all for coming.
cues.zh: 我们已经来到时空的尽头；再次感谢大家到场。

cues.zh: [掌声]
